verses.text: This is the vision Isaiah, Amoz's son, saw about Judah and Jerusalem when Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah were kings of Judah.
Heavens, listen up! Earth, pay attention! The LORD has spoken: “I fed my children and raised them, and they turned against me.
An ox knows its owner, and a donkey knows its master's feeding trough. But Israel doesn't know me. My people don't even stop to think.”

What a sinful nation, weighed down with wrongdoing! You're the offspring of evildoers, children who act corruptly. You've walked out on the LORD and treated the Holy One of Israel with contempt. You've turned your backs and gone far away.
Why take another beating just to rebel even more? Your whole head is sick, and your whole heart is weak.
From the bottom of your foot to the top of your head, there's nothing healthy. Just wounds, welts, and open sores. Nobody's closed them up, wrapped them, or soothed them with oil.
Your country is wrecked. Your cities have burned. Strangers are eating up your land right in front of you, leaving it ruined like land taken over by outsiders.
Daughter Zion is left standing like a shelter in a vineyard, like a hut in a melon field, like a city under siege.
If the LORD of Armies hadn't left a tiny group of us alive, we'd have ended up like Sodom. We'd have been just like Gomorrah.
Listen to the LORD's word, you rulers of Sodom! Hear what our God teaches, you people of Gomorrah!
“What do I want with all these sacrifices?” says the LORD. “I've had enough of rams burned as offerings and the fat of well-fed animals. The blood of bulls, lambs, and male goats doesn't please me.
When you show up in front of me, who asked you to come stomping through my courts?
Quit bringing offerings that mean nothing. Your incense disgusts me. Your New Moons, Sabbaths, and gatherings are more than I can stand when there's evil in the assembly.
I hate your New Moons and your scheduled feasts with my whole soul. They're a load on me, and I'm tired of carrying it.
When you spread your hands out, I'll look away. Pray all you want. I won't listen. Your hands are covered in blood.
Wash up. Get clean. Get the evil you're doing out of my sight. Stop doing wrong.
Learn to do good. Go after justice. Help the people being oppressed. Defend children without fathers. Speak up for widows.”
“Come on, let's talk this through,” says the LORD. “Even if your sins are scarlet, they'll be white like snow. Even if they're red like crimson, they'll be like wool.
If you're willing to listen and obey, you'll eat the good things this land grows.
If you refuse and rebel, the sword will devour you.” The LORD himself has spoken.
How did the faithful city become a prostitute? It used to be full of justice. People did what was right there. Now murderers live there.
Your silver has turned to waste metal. Your wine is watered down.
Your rulers are rebels who run with thieves. Every one of them loves a bribe and chases payouts. They don't defend children without fathers, and a widow's case never even gets heard.
So the Lord, GOD of Armies, the Mighty One of Israel, says, “I'll get relief from those who oppose me and take vengeance on my enemies.
I'll turn my hand against you, clean out all your waste metal, and take away all your tin.
I'll bring back your judges like you had at first and your advisers like you had at the beginning. After that, people will call you ‘the city that does right, the faithful town.’
Zion will be bought back through justice, and the people who turn back to her through righteousness.
But rebels and sinners will fall together. The people who walk away from the LORD will be consumed.
You'll be ashamed of the oaks you wanted so badly, and humiliated over the gardens you chose.
You'll be like an oak with leaves that wither, like a garden without water.
The strong will be like dry tinder, and what they've done will be the spark. They'll both burn together, and nobody will put it out.”
Here's what Isaiah, Amoz's son, saw about Judah and Jerusalem.
In the days to come, the mountain where the LORD's house stands will be set above all the mountains, lifted higher than the hills. All the nations will stream toward it.

Many peoples will say, “Come on, let's go up to the LORD's mountain, to the house of Jacob's God. He'll teach us how he wants us to live, and we'll walk his paths.” His teaching will go out from Zion and the LORD's word from Jerusalem.

He'll settle disputes between nations and give rulings for many peoples. They'll hammer their swords into plow blades and their spears into pruning hooks. Nations won't raise swords against each other or train for war anymore.
Family of Jacob, come on. Let's walk in the LORD's light.
You've left your people, the family of Jacob. They've filled themselves with ways from the east, practice divination like the Philistines, and shake hands on deals with foreigners.
Their land is packed with silver and gold, and there's no end to their treasure. It's packed with horses, and there's no end to their chariots.
Their land is full of idols too. They bow down to their own handiwork, things their own fingers made.
People are brought low, and humanity is humbled. So don't forgive them.
Get into the rocks and hide in the dust from the terror of the LORD and the glory of his majesty.
People who look down on everybody will be brought low. The arrogant will have to bow. On that day, the LORD alone will be lifted high.
The LORD of Armies has a day coming for everything proud and arrogant, everything lifted up. It's all coming down.
That day is coming for every tall cedar of Lebanon and every oak of Bashan,
for every high mountain and every hill that rises up,
for every tall tower and every fortified wall,
for every ship of Tarshish and every beautiful piece of artwork.
Human pride will bow down and arrogance will be brought low. On that day, the LORD alone will be lifted high.
The idols will disappear completely.
People will run into rocky caves and holes in the ground to hide from the terror of the LORD and the glory of his majesty when he gets up and shakes the earth hard.
On that day people will throw their silver and gold idols to the moles and bats, the very idols they made for themselves to worship.
They'll duck into caves and cracks in the jagged rocks to hide from the terror of the LORD and the glory of his majesty when he gets up and shakes the earth hard.
Stop putting your trust in people. All they've got is breath in their nostrils. How much can you count on them?
Look, the Lord, GOD of Armies, is taking away everything Jerusalem and Judah depend on. All their bread, all their water,
their mighty warriors and soldiers, judges and prophets, fortune-tellers and elders,
commanders over fifty, people held in honor, advisers, skilled craftspeople, and clever spellcasters.
I'll put boys in charge of them, and children will rule over them.
People will oppress each other, neighbors pushing neighbors around. The young will mouth off to the old, and the wicked will disrespect people who deserve honor.
Someone will grab his brother right there in their father's house and say, “You've got clothes. You be our ruler. Take charge of this wreck.”
That day he'll cry out, “I'm no healer. I've got no bread or clothes in my house. Don't make me ruler of these people.”
Jerusalem is wrecked and Judah has fallen. What they say and do goes against the LORD, disrespecting his glory right to his face.
Their faces give them away. They parade their sin like Sodom and don't even try to hide it. Trouble for them! They've brought disaster on themselves.
Tell people who do right that it'll go well for them. They'll get to eat the fruit of what they've done.
Trouble for the wicked! Disaster is on them. What their hands have done will come right back to them.
My people have children pushing them around and women ruling over them. My people, your leaders send you the wrong way and tear up the paths you're supposed to walk.
The LORD gets up to make his case. He stands to judge the peoples.
The LORD will take the elders and leaders of his people to court. “You're the ones who ate up the vineyard. Everything you took from poor people is sitting in your houses.
How dare you crush my people and grind the faces of the poor?” says the Lord, GOD of Armies.
The LORD also said, “Zion's daughters are full of pride. They walk with their necks stretched high, flirting with their eyes, taking tiny steps and jingling the ornaments on their feet.
So the Lord will put sores on the heads of Zion's women, and the LORD will leave their scalps bald.”
On that day the Lord will strip away the finery of their anklets, their headbands and crescent necklaces,
their earrings, bracelets, and veils,
their headdresses, ankle chains, and sashes, their perfume bottles and charms,
their signet rings and nose rings,
their fine robes, capes, cloaks, and purses,
their hand mirrors, fine linen clothes, tiaras, and shawls.
Sweet perfume will give way to a rotten smell. A rope will take the place of a belt. Styled hair will give way to a bald head, fine robes to sackcloth, and beauty to a brand.
Your men will fall by the sword, and your strongest will die in the war.
Her gates will cry and mourn. She'll be left empty, sitting on the ground.
That day seven women will grab one man and say, “We'll buy our own bread and wear our own clothes. Just let us carry your name. Take this shame off us.”
That day the LORD's branch will be beautiful and glorious. What the land grows will be the beauty and pride of the people of Israel who survive.
Everyone left in Zion and everyone who remains in Jerusalem will be called holy, everyone whose name is on the list of the living in Jerusalem.
That's when the Lord will have washed away the filth of Zion's daughters and cleaned the blood out of Jerusalem by a spirit of justice and a spirit of burning.
Then the LORD will make a cloud and smoke by day and a blazing fire by night over every home on Mount Zion and every gathering there. A canopy will cover all that glory.
There'll be a shelter to shade people from the daytime heat, a safe place to get out of the storm and rain.
Let me sing a song for the one I love about his vineyard. My dear one had a vineyard on a hill with rich soil.
He dug it up, cleared out the stones, and planted it with the best vines. He built a watchtower in the middle and cut out a winepress. He waited for good grapes, and all he got was wild ones.
“Now, people of Jerusalem and Judah, you tell me who's in the right, me or my vineyard.
What else could I have done for it that I didn't already do? I waited for good grapes. Why did it only grow wild ones?
Here's what I'll do to my vineyard. I'll pull up its hedge and it'll get eaten up. I'll tear down its wall and it'll get trampled.
I'll leave it a wasteland. No pruning, no hoeing. Briers and thorns will take over. I'll even tell the clouds to hold back their rain.”

The vineyard of the LORD of Armies is the family of Israel, and the people of Judah are the plants he took joy in. He looked for justice and saw oppression. He looked for people doing right and heard cries of distress.
Trouble is coming for you who buy up house after house and take field after field till there's no space left and you're the only ones living in the land.
I heard the LORD of Armies say, “Many houses will stand empty. Even big, beautiful homes won't have anybody living in them.
Ten acres of vines will only yield one bath of wine, and a homer of seed will only give back an ephah of grain.”
Trouble is coming for people who get up early just to go after strong drink and stay up late till wine sets them on fire.
They've got harp, lyre, tambourine, flute, and wine at their feasts, but they don't pay attention to what the LORD is doing. They don't stop to look at what his hands have made.
That's why my people are going into captivity. They don't understand. Their honored people are starving, and the crowds are dried out with thirst.
So the grave has worked up a bigger appetite and opened its mouth wide. Their glory, their crowds, all their show, and everyone partying among them go down into it.
People are brought low. Humanity is humbled, and those arrogant eyes have to look down.
But the LORD of Armies is lifted high through justice, and the Holy God shows his holiness by doing what is right.
Then lambs will graze like they're in their own pasture, and strangers will eat what grows among the ruins of the rich.
Trouble is coming for people who drag their wrongdoing along on strings of lies and haul wickedness like a cart tied to a rope.
They say, “Tell him to hurry up! Let's see him get to work. Let the Holy One of Israel bring his plans on so we can find out what they are!”
Trouble is coming for people who call evil good and good evil, who swap light for darkness and darkness for light, who call what's bitter sweet and what's sweet bitter.
Trouble is coming for people who think they're wise in their own eyes and sure they've got good judgment.
Trouble is coming for people who can drink anyone under the table and call themselves champions at mixing strong drinks,
who let the guilty walk for a bribe and take justice away from the innocent.

Just like fire licks up stubble and dry grass collapses in the flames, their roots will rot and their blossoms will blow away as dust. They threw out the teaching of the LORD of Armies and looked down on the word of the Holy One of Israel.

So the LORD's anger burns against his people. He reached out his hand against them and struck them. The mountains shake, and bodies lie like trash in the streets. Even after all this, his anger hasn't turned away. His hand is still stretched out.
He'll raise a banner for distant nations and whistle for them from the end of the earth. Look how fast they'll come.
None of them will be worn out or stumble. Nobody will nod off or sleep. Not a belt will come loose and not a sandal strap will snap.
Their arrows are sharp and every bow is drawn. Their horses' hooves are hard as flint and their wheels spin like a whirlwind.
They'll roar like a lioness, like young lions. They'll roar and grab their prey and carry it away, and nobody will rescue it.
That day they'll roar against the people like the sea. Look toward the land and all you'll see is darkness and distress. Even the light goes dark behind the clouds.
The year King Uzziah died, I saw the Lord sitting way up high on a throne. The train of his robe filled the temple.
Above him stood the seraphim. Each had six wings. Two covered their faces, two covered their feet, and two kept them flying.
They called out to one another, “Holy, holy, holy is the LORD of Armies! The whole earth is full of his glory!”
At the sound of that voice, the doorways shook right down to their foundations, and smoke filled the temple.
I said, “I'm done for! My lips are unclean, and I live with people whose lips are unclean. And I've seen the King, the LORD of Armies, with my own eyes!”
Then one of the seraphim flew right over to me with a glowing coal in his hand. He'd picked it up from the altar with tongs.
He touched my mouth with it and said, “Look, this touched your lips. Your guilt is gone, and your sin is forgiven.”
Then I heard the Lord say, “Who am I going to send? Who will go for us?” I said, “Here I am. Send me!”
He said, “Go tell these people, ‘You're hearing, all right, but you don't understand. You're seeing, all right, but you don't get what you're seeing.’
Make these people's hearts dull, their ears heavy, and their eyes shut. Otherwise they might see with their eyes, hear with their ears, understand with their hearts, and turn back and be healed.”
I said, “Lord, how long?” He said, “Till the cities are wrecked with nobody living in them, the houses are empty, and the whole land is a wasteland,
till the LORD has sent people far away and abandoned places fill the land.
Even if a tenth is left, that too will be consumed. A terebinth or an oak leaves a stump when it's cut down. The holy seed is that stump.”
Ahaz was king of Judah, the son of Jotham and grandson of Uzziah. In his day, King Rezin of Syria and King Pekah of Israel, Remaliah's son, marched up to fight Jerusalem, but they couldn't take it.
Word reached David's household: “Syria has teamed up with Ephraim.” Ahaz and his people shook inside the way forest trees shake in the wind.
The LORD said to Isaiah, “Go meet Ahaz with your son Shearjashub. You'll find him at the end of the channel from the upper pool, on the road to the cloth washer's field.
Tell him, ‘Watch yourself and stay calm. Don't be scared or lose heart over these two smoking ends of burned-out torches, no matter how furious Rezin and Syria or Remaliah's son get.
Syria, Ephraim, and Remaliah's son have made plans to hurt you. They're saying,
“Let's march up against Judah and rip it apart, split it between us, and put Tabeel's son on the throne.”
But here's what the Lord GOD says: “That plan won't stand. It won't happen.”
Damascus is the head of Syria, and Rezin is the head of Damascus. Within sixty-five years Ephraim will be smashed to pieces and won't be a people anymore.
Samaria is the head of Ephraim, and Remaliah's son is the head of Samaria. If you won't believe, you won't stand firm.’”
The LORD spoke to Ahaz again.
“Ask the LORD your God for a sign. Ask for one from the depths below or the heights above.”
Ahaz said, “I won't ask. I won't put the LORD to the test.”
Isaiah said, “Listen up, family of David. Is wearing people out not enough for you? Are you going to wear out my God's patience too?
So the Lord himself will give you a sign. Look, the virgin will become pregnant, have a son, and name him Immanuel.
He'll eat butter and honey by the time he knows how to say no to evil and choose good.
Before the child knows how to say no to evil and choose good, the land of those two kings you can't stand will be deserted.
The LORD will bring on you, your people, and your father's household days like nothing since Ephraim broke away from Judah. He'll bring the king of Assyria.”
That day the LORD will whistle for the fly from the far ends of Egypt's rivers and for the bee from Assyria.
They'll all come and settle in the empty valleys, in the cracks in the rocks, on every thorn hedge, and in every pasture.
That day the Lord will use a razor hired from beyond the River, the king of Assyria, to shave the hair from head to foot and take off the beard too.
That day someone will keep a young cow and two sheep alive.
They'll give so much milk that he'll eat butter. Everyone left in the land will live on butter and honey.
That day every place that once had a thousand vines worth a thousand silver shekels will be overrun with briers and thorns.
People will go there with bows and arrows because the whole land will be covered in briers and thorns.
You won't go near the hills you used to hoe, afraid of the briers and thorns. Those hills will be places to turn oxen loose and let sheep roam.
The LORD told me, “Get a big tablet and write on it with an ordinary pen, ‘For Maher Shalal Hash Baz.’
I'll get two trustworthy witnesses to testify for me, Uriah the priest and Zechariah, Jeberechiah's son.”
I went to the prophetess, and she became pregnant and had a son. Then the LORD said, “Name him Maher Shalal Hash Baz.
Before the child can say ‘My father’ or ‘My mother,’ the king of Assyria will carry off Damascus's riches and the loot from Samaria.”
The LORD spoke to me again.
“These people turned down the gentle waters of Shiloah and got excited about Rezin and Remaliah's son.
So now look. The Lord is bringing the mighty floodwaters of the River against them, the king of Assyria and all his glory. The water will fill every channel and spill over every bank.
It'll sweep into Judah, flooding its way through till it reaches your neck. Its wings will spread across the whole width of your land, Immanuel.
Make all the noise you want, you peoples. You'll be smashed to pieces! Listen, all you far-off countries. Get ready for battle and be shattered! Get ready for battle and be shattered!
Make your plans together and they'll come to nothing. Say what you're going to do and it won't stand, because God is with us.”
The LORD spoke to me with a strong hand on me and told me to stay off the road these people were taking. He said,
“Don't call everything a conspiracy just because these people do. Don't be afraid of what scares them. Don't let it terrify you.
Treat the LORD of Armies as holy. He's the one you should fear. He's the one you should stand in dread of.
He'll be a sanctuary. But to both houses of Israel he'll be a stone they trip over and a rock that brings them down. To the people of Jerusalem he'll be a trap and a snare.
Many will stumble over it and fall. They'll be broken, caught in the trap, and taken.”
Wrap up the covenant. Seal the teaching among my disciples.
I'll wait for the LORD, even while he hides his face from Jacob's family. I'll keep looking for him.
Look, the children the LORD gave me and I are signs and wonders in Israel from the LORD of Armies, who lives on Mount Zion.
When people tell you, “Go ask the mediums and the wizards who chirp and mutter,” shouldn't people ask their God? Why ask the dead for answers for the living?
Back to the teaching and the covenant! If what they say doesn't line up with this word, there's no dawn for them.
They'll wander through the land, worn down and hungry. When hunger hits, they'll get worked up and curse their king and their God. They'll look up,
then look down at the earth and see trouble, darkness, and the gloom of anguish. They'll be driven into deep darkness.

But the land that was in pain won't stay in the dark. Before, he brought shame on the lands of Zebulun and Naphtali. Later he made them glorious, along the road by the sea, across the Jordan, in Galilee of the nations.
People walking in darkness have seen a great light. Light has reached the people living in the land under death's shadow.
You've made the nation grow and given them more joy. They celebrate in front of you like people bringing in a harvest, like people dividing up what they won.
You broke the yoke that weighed them down, the bar across their shoulders, the rod of the one who oppressed them, just like on the day of Midian.
All the gear carried into the roar of battle and all the clothes rolled in blood will burn. They'll be fuel for the fire.
A child is born to us. A son is given to us. The weight of ruling will rest on his shoulders. He'll be called Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace.

His rule will keep growing, and his peace will never end. On David's throne he'll set his kingdom firm and hold it up with justice and righteousness from then on, forever. The LORD of Armies will make this happen with his own zeal.
The Lord sent a word against Jacob, and it came down on Israel.
All the people will know it, including Ephraim and the people of Samaria. In their pride, they say,
“The bricks fell, but we'll build again with cut stone. They chopped down the sycamore figs, but we'll put cedars in their place.”
So the LORD will raise Rezin's adversaries against Israel and stir up Israel's enemies.
The Syrians in front and the Philistines behind will open their mouths and devour Israel. Even after all this, his anger hasn't turned away. His hand is still stretched out.
But the people haven't turned back to the one who struck them. They haven't gone looking for the LORD of Armies.
So the LORD will cut off Israel's head and tail, palm branch and reed, all in one day.
The elder and the person everybody honors are the head. The prophet who teaches lies is the tail.
The people in charge lead everybody off course, and the people who follow them end up ruined.

So the Lord won't take joy in their young men or show compassion to their children without fathers and their widows. Everyone acts like nothing is sacred and does wrong, and every mouth talks foolishness. Even after all this, his anger hasn't turned away. His hand is still stretched out.
Wickedness burns like fire. It eats up the briers and thorns, sets the thick forest on fire, and sends smoke rolling up in a column.
The anger of the LORD of Armies burns up the land. The people themselves are fuel for the fire. Nobody spares even their own brother.
They'll tear into what's on their right and still be hungry. They'll eat what's on their left and still want more. Everyone will eat the flesh of their own arm.
Manasseh will eat Ephraim, Ephraim will eat Manasseh, and both will turn against Judah. Even after all this, his anger hasn't turned away. His hand is still stretched out.
Trouble is coming for people who pass crooked laws and write rules that crush others,
taking justice away from people in need and stealing the rights of the poor among my people, so they can rob widows and prey on children without fathers.
What will you do when the day of reckoning comes and disaster hits from far away? Who will you run to for help? Where will you stash your wealth?
You'll have nowhere to go but down among the prisoners or under the bodies of the dead. Even after all this, his anger hasn't turned away. His hand is still stretched out.
Trouble for Assyria, the rod of my anger! The staff in its hand carries my fury.
I'll send him against a nation that treats nothing as sacred. I'll order him to strip the people who make me angry, take what he wants, and trample them like mud in the street.
But that's not what he thinks he's doing. That's not the plan in his heart. What he wants is to wipe out nations, and plenty of them.
He says, “Aren't all my commanders kings?
Is Calno any different from Carchemish? Hamath from Arpad? Samaria from Damascus?”
My hand reached kingdoms full of idols, with carved images that outdid the ones in Jerusalem and Samaria.
Won't I do to Jerusalem and her idols exactly what I did to Samaria and hers?
When the Lord finishes everything he means to do on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem, he'll punish what grew out of the king of Assyria's stubborn pride and that arrogant look on his face.

The king said, “I did it with my own strength and my own wisdom. I know what I'm doing. I moved the borders of whole peoples and robbed their treasuries. I brought their rulers down like a mighty warrior.
I reached into a nest and found all the wealth of the peoples. I gathered up the whole earth the way you pick up abandoned eggs. Nobody flapped a wing, opened a mouth, or let out a chirp.”

Does an ax get to brag over the person swinging it? Does a saw get to act bigger than the person using it? That's like a rod picking up the person holding it, or a wooden staff lifting somebody who's no piece of wood.
That's why the Lord, GOD of Armies, will make his well-fed ones waste away. A blaze will catch under all his glory and burn like fire.
Israel's light will become a fire, and Israel's Holy One a flame. It'll burn through all his thorns and briers in a single day.
He'll burn up the glory of the forest and the rich fields, body and soul. It'll be like a flag bearer collapsing.
So few trees will be left in his forest that a child could write down the number.
That day those left of Israel and the people who escaped from Jacob's family won't lean on the one who struck them anymore. They'll truly lean on the LORD, the Holy One of Israel.
A remnant will come back. Those left of Jacob will come back to the mighty God.
Israel, even if your people are as countless as sand by the sea, only a remnant will return. Destruction has been decided, and it will overflow with righteousness.
The Lord, GOD of Armies, will carry out the full destruction he's determined across the whole earth.
So the Lord, GOD of Armies, says, “My people who live in Zion, don't be scared of the Assyrian, even if he hits you with a rod and raises his staff against you like Egypt did.
In just a little while my anger against you will have run its course. Then I'll turn my anger on him to destroy him.”
The LORD of Armies will raise a whip against him, like when Midian was slaughtered at the rock of Oreb. His rod will reach over the sea, and he'll raise it like he did against Egypt.
That day his load will come off your shoulders and his yoke off your neck. The yoke will break because of the anointing oil.
He's reached Aiath and passed through Migron. He's storing his baggage at Michmash.
They've crossed the pass and stopped for the night at Geba. Ramah is shaking. Saul's Gibeah has run away.
Cry out loud, daughter of Gallim! Listen, Laishah! Poor Anathoth!
Madmenah is on the run. The people of Gebim are fleeing to safety.
Today he'll stop at Nob and shake his fist at the mountain of daughter Zion, the hill of Jerusalem.
Look, the Lord, GOD of Armies, will chop off the branches with terrifying force. The tall ones will be cut down, and the ones that tower overhead will come low.
He'll hack through the thick forest with iron, and Lebanon will fall at the hand of the Mighty One.
A new shoot will come up from Jesse's stump, and a branch from his roots will grow fruit.
The LORD's Spirit will rest on him, the spirit of wisdom and understanding, of good counsel and strength, of knowledge and reverence for the LORD.
He'll take joy in standing in awe of the LORD. He won't judge from what his eyes happen to see or make decisions from what his ears happen to hear.
He'll judge poor people by what's right and give the humble of the earth a fair hearing. His words will strike the earth like a rod, and the breath from his lips will put the wicked to death.
He'll wear righteousness like a belt around his waist, with faithfulness strapped on tight.
The wolf will live with the lamb. The leopard will lie down with the young goat. The calf, the young lion, and the fattened calf will all be together, and a little child will lead them.
The cow and the bear will graze together and their young will lie down side by side. The lion will eat straw like an ox.
A nursing baby will play by a cobra's hole, and a child who's just been weaned will put their hand over a viper's den.
No one will harm or destroy anywhere on my holy mountain. The earth will be full of knowing the LORD the way water fills the sea.
That day the nations will seek the root of Jesse. He'll stand like a banner for the peoples, and his resting place will be glorious.
That day the Lord will reach out his hand a second time to bring back the people he has left in Assyria, Egypt, Pathros, Cush, Elam, Shinar, Hamath, and the islands of the sea.
He'll raise a banner for the nations and gather Israel's outcasts. He'll bring the scattered people of Judah together from all four corners of the earth.
Ephraim's jealousy will go away, and the people who harass Judah will be cut off. Ephraim won't envy Judah, and Judah won't harass Ephraim.

They'll swoop down on the slopes of the Philistine lands to the west. Together they'll take plunder from the people of the east. They'll reach out and take power over Edom and Moab, and the people of Ammon will obey them.
The LORD will dry up the tongue of the Egyptian sea. He'll wave his hand over the River with a scorching wind, split it into seven streams, and let people walk across in their sandals.
There'll be a highway from Assyria for those of his people who are left, like the road Israel had when they came up out of Egypt.
That day you'll say, “Thank you, LORD. You were angry with me, but your anger has turned away and now you comfort me.
Look, God is the one who saves me. I'll trust him and won't be scared. The LORD, the LORD is my strength and my song. He's become my salvation.”
You'll draw water with joy from the wells of salvation.
That day you'll say, “Thank the LORD! Call on his name! Tell the peoples what he's done! Tell them how high his name is lifted!
Sing to the LORD! He's done amazing things. Let the whole earth hear about it!
People of Zion, raise your voices and shout! The Holy One of Israel is great right there among you!”
This is the message about Babylon that Isaiah, Amoz's son, saw.
Raise a banner on the bare mountain! Shout to them! Wave them on so they go through the gates of the nobles.
I've given orders to the ones I set apart. I've called my mighty warriors to carry out my anger, the ones who celebrate proudly.
Listen to that crowd in the mountains! It sounds like a whole people on the move. Hear the uproar of kingdoms and nations gathering! The LORD of Armies is calling up his army for battle.
They're coming from a far country, from the farthest edge of the sky. The LORD is coming with the weapons of his fury to destroy the whole land.
Cry out! The LORD's day is close. It'll come as destruction from the Almighty.
Every hand will go weak, and everybody's courage will melt away.
They'll be horrified. Pain and grief will grab them like contractions in childbirth. They'll stare at each other in shock, their faces like flames.
Look, the day of the LORD is coming, cruel with rage and fierce anger. It'll leave the land wrecked and wipe its sinners out of it.
The stars and constellations won't give their light. The sun will come up dark, and the moon won't shine.
I'll punish the world for its evil and the wicked for what they've done. I'll put an end to the pride of the arrogant and bring the swagger of ruthless people down.
I'll make people harder to find than fine gold, a person rarer than pure gold from Ophir.
So I'll make the heavens shake and the earth lurch out of place in the fury of the LORD of Armies, on the day his anger burns.
Like a gazelle being hunted, like sheep with nobody to gather them, people will turn back to their own people and run to their own land.
Everyone they find will be pierced through. Everyone they catch will fall by the sword.
Their babies will be killed right in front of them. Their homes will be ransacked, and their wives raped.
Look, I'll stir up the Medes against them. Silver means nothing to them, and gold won't tempt them.
Their bows will strike down the young men. They won't have pity on babies in the womb or spare children when they see them.
Babylon, the glory of kingdoms and the beautiful pride of the Chaldeans, will end up like Sodom and Gomorrah when God overthrew them.
Nobody will ever live there again, generation after generation. No Arabian will pitch a tent there, and no shepherd will settle a flock there to rest.
Desert animals will lie down there, and jackals will fill the houses. Ostriches will live there, and wild goats will leap around.
Hyenas will howl in the fortresses and jackals in the lovely palaces. Babylon's time is close. Her days won't be stretched out.
The LORD will have compassion on Jacob. He'll choose Israel again and settle them on their own land. Foreigners will join them and become part of Jacob's household.

Other peoples will bring them back to their home. In the LORD's land the people of Israel will take them as servants, men and women. They'll take their former captors captive and rule over the ones who oppressed them.
The day the LORD gives you a break from your pain, your trouble, and the hard labor you were forced to do,
you'll take up this taunt against the king of Babylon: “Look how the oppressor has stopped! The golden city is finished!”
The LORD snapped the staff of the wicked and the scepter of the rulers.
They hit peoples over and over in their rage and ruled nations in anger, persecuting them with nobody to hold them back.
The whole earth finally rests. Everything goes quiet, and then the people burst into song.
Even the cypresses and the cedars of Lebanon celebrate with you. “Now that you've been brought low, no one comes up here to cut us down.”
The grave below is stirring to meet you when you come. It wakes the spirits of the dead, all the rulers of the earth. It gets the kings of the nations up off their thrones.
They'll all ask you, “So you got weak like us too? You ended up just like us?”
Your grand show and the sound of your stringed instruments came down to the grave with you. Maggots are laid out beneath you, and worms are your covers.
How far you've fallen from heaven, shining one, son of the dawn! You've been cut down to the ground, you who brought nations down!
You told yourself, “I'll climb up to heaven! I'll lift my throne above God's stars. I'll sit on the mountain where they gather, way up in the north.
I'll climb higher than the tops of the clouds. I'll make myself like the Most High!”
But you'll be dragged down to the grave, to the deepest part of the pit.
People who see you will stare and think it over. “Is this the guy who made the earth tremble and shook kingdoms,
who turned the world into a wilderness and tore down its cities, who wouldn't let his prisoners go home?”
All the kings of the nations rest in glory, each in his own resting place.
But you've been thrown out of your tomb like a branch nobody wants, covered with bodies pierced by swords that go down among the stones of the pit, like a corpse trampled underfoot.
You won't be buried with them. You wrecked your land and killed your own people. The children of evildoers won't have their names remembered forever.
Get ready to put his children to death for the wrongdoing of their fathers, so they won't rise up to take the earth and cover the world with cities.
“I'll rise up against them,” says the LORD of Armies. “I'll wipe out Babylon's name, its survivors, its children, and its grandchildren,” says the LORD.
“I'll turn it into a place for porcupines and pools of water. I'll sweep it away with the broom of destruction,” says the LORD of Armies.
The LORD of Armies has sworn, “What I've decided will happen. What I've planned will stand.
I'll break the Assyrian in my own land and trample him on my mountains. Then his yoke will come off my people and his load will come off their shoulders.
That's the plan set for the whole earth. That's the hand stretched out over every nation.
The LORD of Armies has made his plan. Who can stop it? His hand is stretched out. Who can push it back?”
This message came the year King Ahaz died.
Don't celebrate, Philistia, just because the rod that hit you broke. From that snake's root a viper will come up, and its offspring will be a fiery flying snake.
The firstborn of the poor will have food, and people in need will lie down safely. But I'll kill your root with famine, and the ones you have left will be killed.
Howl, gate! Cry out, city! All of you in Philistia are melting with fear. Smoke is coming out of the north, and nobody in his ranks is falling behind.
What answer will they give the nation's messengers? The LORD founded Zion, and the suffering among his people will find shelter there.
This is the message about Moab. In one night Ar in Moab was wrecked and brought to nothing. In one night Kir in Moab was wrecked and brought to nothing.
They went up to Bayith and Dibon, up to the high places to cry. Moab wails over Nebo and Medeba. Every head is shaved, and every beard is cut off.
People put on sackcloth in the streets. Out in the streets and up on the rooftops, everybody is wailing and crying hard.
Heshbon and Elealeh cry out, and their voices reach all the way to Jahaz. That's why even Moab's armed men cry out. They're shaking inside.
My heart cries for Moab! Her nobles run to Zoar and Eglath Shelishiyah. They go up the road to Luhith in tears and cry out over the destruction on the road to Horonaim.
The waters of Nimrim will be gone. The grass has dried up, the new shoots have died, and there's nothing green left.
So they'll carry what they've gained and everything they've stored up across the Brook of the Willows.
The crying has gone all around Moab's borders. You can hear its wailing at Eglaim and all the way to Beer Elim.
Dimon's waters are full of blood, and I'll bring even more trouble on Dimon. A lion will come for the people who escape Moab and for whoever is left in the land.
Send lambs for the ruler of the land, from Selah across the wilderness to the mountain of daughter Zion.
At the crossings of the Arnon, the daughters of Moab will be like birds that can't find their way, like a nest that's been scattered.
Give advice! Make a fair decision! Give us shade as dark as night in the middle of the day. Hide the outcasts. Don't hand over the people on the run.
Let my outcasts stay with you. Give Moab somewhere to hide from the destroyer. The one who squeezed people for money is finished. The destruction stops, and the oppressors are gone from the land.
A throne will stand firm in faithful love. Someone trustworthy will sit on it in David's tent, judging fairly, seeking justice, and quick to do what's right.
We've heard how proud Moab is, full of arrogance, pride, and rage. All that bragging comes to nothing.
So Moab will cry for Moab. Everybody will wail. You'll grieve over the raisin cakes of Kir Hareseth, crushed by what's happened.

The fields of Heshbon and the vines of Sibmah are drying up. The rulers of the nations broke down those prized branches that reached Jazer and trailed out into the wilderness. Their shoots spread far and even crossed the sea.
So I'll cry with Jazer over the vines of Sibmah. Heshbon and Elealeh, I'll drench you with my tears. The battle shout has come down on your summer fruit and your harvest.
Joy and laughter have been taken out of the fruitful fields. Nobody's singing or cheering in the vineyards. Nobody's pressing grapes into wine. I've stopped the shouting.
That's why my heart sounds like a harp for Moab, and everything inside me aches for Kir Heres.
When Moab goes up to the high place and wears himself out, then comes to his sanctuary to pray, it won't get him anywhere.
That's the word the LORD spoke about Moab before.
Now the LORD says, “Within three years, counted as exactly as a hired worker counts a contract, all of Moab's glory and its great crowds will be brought to shame. The few who remain will be weak.”
This is the message about Damascus. “Look, Damascus won't be a city anymore. It'll be a pile of ruins.
The towns of Aroer are deserted. Flocks will take them over and lie down there with nobody to scare them off.
Ephraim will lose its fortress, Damascus will lose its kingdom, and the survivors of Syria will be like what's left of Israel's glory,” says the LORD of Armies.
“That day Jacob's glory will waste away. His once well-fed body will go thin.
It'll be like a harvester gathering wheat and cutting the grain with his arm. It'll be like picking up the last bits of grain in the valley of Rephaim.

Still, a little will be left. Shake an olive tree and you'll find two or three olives at the top of the highest branch, four or five out on the ends of the branches of a tree that bore fruit,” says the LORD, Israel's God.
That day people will turn to the one who made them and look with reverence to the Holy One of Israel.
They won't look to the altars they built with their own hands or honor what their own fingers made, whether it's the Asherah poles or the incense altars.
That day their fortified towns will be like abandoned places in the woods and on the mountaintops, places people left when Israel came. Everything will be deserted.
You've forgotten the God who saves you. You didn't remember the rock that gives you strength. So you plant lovely plants and put in seedlings from abroad.
The day you plant them, you put a hedge around them. By morning you get your seed to bloom. But the harvest disappears on the day of grief and unbearable pain.
Listen to all those peoples in an uproar, roaring like the sea! Hear the nations rushing in like a flood of mighty water!
The nations will rush in like a flood, but he'll call them down and they'll run far away. They'll be chased off like husks blown across the mountains or dust spinning ahead of a storm.
By evening, look, terror! Before morning they're gone. That's what the people who plunder us get, the share of those who rob us.
Ah, land of rustling wings beyond the rivers of Ethiopia!

You send ambassadors by sea in boats made of papyrus. You say, “Go, quick messengers, to a tall, smooth-skinned nation, a people feared from the beginning till now, a nation that measures out and tramples down, a land cut through by rivers!”
Everybody who lives on earth, look up when a banner goes up on the mountains! Listen when the trumpet blows!
The LORD told me, “I'll stay still and watch from where I live, like clear heat in sunshine, like a cloud of dew in the heat of harvest.”
Before harvest, when the flowers have dropped and the blossoms have become ripening grapes, he'll snip off the shoots with pruning hooks and cut away the spreading branches.
They'll all be left for the mountain birds of prey and the animals of the earth. The birds will feed on them in summer, and the animals will feed on them in winter.

At that time the tall, smooth-skinned people, feared from the beginning till now, the nation that measures out and tramples down, whose land the rivers divide, will bring a gift to the LORD of Armies at Mount Zion, the place that bears his name.
This is the message about Egypt. “Look, the LORD comes to Egypt riding on a fast-moving cloud. Egypt's idols will shake in his presence, and Egypt's courage will melt away.
I'll turn Egyptians against Egyptians. They'll fight brother against brother, neighbor against neighbor, city against city, kingdom against kingdom.
Egypt will lose heart. I'll wreck their plans, and they'll turn to idols, spellcasters, mediums, and wizards.
I'll hand the Egyptians over to a cruel master. A fierce king will rule them,” says the Lord, GOD of Armies.
The waters of the sea will run out, and the river will dry up and go to waste.
The rivers will stink. Egypt's streams will shrink and dry up. The reeds and rushes will wither.
The meadows right along the Nile and all the fields planted beside it will dry up, blow away, and disappear.
The fishers will grieve. Everyone who drops a line in the Nile will mourn, and those who spread their nets on the water will lose heart.
People who work with combed flax and people who weave white cloth will be at a loss.
The pillars will be smashed, and everyone who works for a wage will be crushed inside.
The rulers of Zoan are complete fools. Even Pharaoh's wisest advisers give foolish advice. How can you tell Pharaoh, “I come from wise men. I'm descended from ancient kings”?
So where are your wise men? Let them tell you now. Let them figure out what the LORD of Armies has planned for Egypt.
Zoan's rulers have become fools. Memphis's rulers have been fooled. The very people who were meant to hold Egypt's tribes together have led it off course.
The LORD has mixed a spirit of confusion into Egypt. They've sent Egypt staggering in everything it does, like a drunk stumbling in his own vomit.
Nobody in Egypt will be able to get anything done, head or tail, palm branch or reed.
That day the Egyptians will be like women trembling in fear as the LORD of Armies shakes his hand over them.
Judah will terrify Egypt. Just hearing its name will scare people because of what the LORD of Armies has planned against Egypt.
That day five cities in Egypt will speak the language of Canaan and swear loyalty to the LORD of Armies. One will be called “The City of Destruction.”
That day there'll be an altar to the LORD in the middle of Egypt and a pillar to the LORD at its border.
They'll be a sign and a witness to the LORD of Armies in Egypt. When people cry to the LORD because they're being oppressed, he'll send them a savior and defender who'll rescue them.
The LORD will make himself known to Egypt, and that day Egyptians will know the LORD. They'll worship with sacrifices and offerings, make vows to him, and keep those vows.
The LORD will strike Egypt, then heal it. They'll come back to the LORD, he'll listen to their pleas, and he'll heal them.
That day there'll be a highway from Egypt to Assyria. Assyrians will come into Egypt, Egyptians will go into Assyria, and they'll worship together.
That day Israel will stand alongside Egypt and Assyria as the third, a blessing in the middle of the earth.
The LORD of Armies will bless them and say, “Blessed be Egypt, my people, Assyria, the work of my hands, and Israel, my inheritance.”
That was the year Sargon, king of Assyria, sent Tartan to Ashdod. Tartan attacked the city and took it.
Around then the LORD spoke through Isaiah, Amoz's son. “Go, take the sackcloth off your waist and the sandals off your feet.” Isaiah did it and walked around naked and barefoot.
The LORD said, “My servant Isaiah has walked naked and barefoot for three years as a sign and a wonder about Egypt and Ethiopia.
That's how the king of Assyria will march away Egypt's captives and Ethiopia's exiles, young and old, naked and barefoot with their backsides showing, to Egypt's shame.
People will be horrified and humiliated over Ethiopia, where they put their hope, and Egypt, where they took pride.
That day the people along this coast will say, ‘Look at what happened to the ones we counted on! We ran to them for help against the king of Assyria. How are we supposed to escape now?’”
This is the message about the wilderness of the sea. It comes from the wilderness, from a terrifying land, sweeping in like whirlwinds in the South.
I've been shown a brutal vision. The traitor betrays and the destroyer destroys. Go up, Elam! Attack! I've put an end to all of Media's sighing.
Pain grips my body like a woman in labor. It hurts so much I can't hear. I'm so shaken I can't see.
My heart won't settle. Horror has me scared. The evening I was looking forward to has me trembling now.
They set the table and post the guard. They eat and drink. Get up, you rulers! Oil your shields!
The Lord told me, “Go put someone on watch. Have him report what he sees.
When he sees a troop of riders in pairs, a troop of donkeys, and a troop of camels, he needs to listen closely and stay alert.”
He roared like a lion, “Lord, I'm up on the watchtower all day long, and I stay at my post every night.
Look, riders are coming, two by two!” Then he answered, “Babylon has fallen! Fallen! All the carved images of her gods lie smashed on the ground.
You, my people, have been threshed like grain on my floor!” I've told you what I heard from the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel.
This is the message about Dumah. Someone calls to me from Seir, “Watchman, how much of the night is left? Watchman, how much longer?”
The watchman says, “Morning is coming, and so is night. If you've got questions, ask. Come back again.”
This is the message about Arabia. Caravans of Dedan, you'll spend the night in Arabia's thickets.
The people of Tema brought water to those who were thirsty and came out with bread to meet the people running for their lives.
They were running from swords, from the sword already drawn, the bow already bent, and the heat of battle.
The Lord told me, “Within a year, counted as exactly as a hired worker counts a contract, all of Kedar's glory will be gone.
Only a few of Kedar's mighty archers will be left. The LORD, the God of Israel, has spoken.”
This is the message about the Valley of Vision. What's going on with you? Why has everybody gone up on the roofs?
You're usually so loud, a city buzzing with noise and a town full of joy. But your dead weren't killed by the sword. They didn't die in battle.
Your rulers all ran off together, and the archers tied them up. Everybody found there was taken prisoner together, though they'd fled far away.
So I said, “Look away. Let me cry my heart out. Don't try to cheer me up over what's happened to the daughter of my people.
The Lord, GOD of Armies, has brought a day of panic, trampling, and confusion to the Valley of Vision. Walls are coming down and cries are going up to the mountains.”
Elam came with quivers, chariots full of men, and riders on horses. Kir pulled the covers off its shields.
Your best valleys filled up with chariots, and the horsemen lined up at the gate.
He stripped away Judah's protection. That day you turned to the weapons in the House of the Forest.
You saw all the gaps in the walls of David's city and gathered water from the lower pool.
You counted the houses in Jerusalem and pulled some down to strengthen the wall.
You even built a reservoir between the two walls for water from the old pool. But you never looked to the one who brought all this about or gave any thought to the one who planned it long ago.
That day the Lord, GOD of Armies, called you to cry and grieve, to shave your heads and put on sackcloth.
But look at you celebrating! You're slaughtering cattle and sheep, eating meat, and drinking wine. “Let's eat and drink, because tomorrow we're dead.”
The LORD of Armies spoke right into my ears. “This wrongdoing won't be forgiven you as long as you live,” says the Lord, GOD of Armies.
The Lord, GOD of Armies, says, “Go see Shebna, that treasurer in charge of the household, and tell him,
‘What are you doing here? Who gave you the right to carve yourself a tomb here?’ There he is, carving out his tomb up high, chiseling himself a place in the rock!”
Look, the LORD will get a firm grip on you and hurl you away with force.
He'll wind you up tight and throw you like a ball into a wide-open country. That's where you'll die, and that's where your fancy chariots will end up, you disgrace to your master's household.
I'll throw you out of office, and you'll be pulled down from your position.
That day I'll call for my servant Eliakim, Hilkiah's son.
I'll dress him in your robe, fasten your belt on him, and hand your authority over to him. He'll be like a father to the people of Jerusalem and the household of Judah.
I'll place the key to David's house on his shoulder. What he opens, nobody will shut. What he shuts, nobody will open.
I'll drive him in like a peg in a solid place. He'll be a seat of honor for his father's household.
They'll hang all the glory of his father's house on him, the children and their descendants, every little vessel from the cups to all the pitchers.
“That day,” says the LORD of Armies, “the peg you thought was driven in solid will give way. It'll be cut down and fall, and the load hanging on it will come crashing down.” The LORD has spoken.
This is the message about Tyre. Cry out, ships of Tarshish! Tyre is wrecked. There's no house left and nowhere to come in. The news reaches the ships from Kittim.
Go quiet, you people of the coast, you who were supplied by the merchants of Sidon who crossed the sea.
Across those great waters came grain from the Shihor, the Nile's harvest that made her rich. She was the marketplace of nations.
Hang your head, Sidon. The sea has spoken, the fortress of the sea: “I've never been in labor or given birth. I haven't raised young men or brought up young women.”
When Egypt hears what happened to Tyre, the news will leave them in anguish.
Cross over to Tarshish! Cry out, you who live on the coast!
Is this your party city, the one that's been around since ancient days, that traveled so far on her own feet?
Who planned this against Tyre, the city that handed out crowns, whose merchants were like princes and whose traders were honored all over the earth?
The LORD of Armies planned it. He'll stain the pride of all that glory and bring down the people everyone on earth held in honor.
Daughter of Tarshish, flow through your land like the Nile. There's nothing holding you back anymore.
He stretched his hand over the sea and shook kingdoms. The LORD gave the order to wreck Canaan's fortresses.
He said, “Your celebrating is over, virgin daughter of Sidon. You've been crushed. Get up and cross over to Kittim. You won't get any rest there either.”
Look at the land of the Chaldeans. That people didn't exist before. The Assyrians set it up for desert dwellers. They put up towers, knocked down its palaces, and left it in ruins.
Cry out, ships of Tarshish! Your stronghold has been wrecked.
That day Tyre will be forgotten for seventy years, the length of one king's days. At the end of seventy years, Tyre's story will be like the song about the prostitute.
“Pick up a harp and walk around the city, you forgotten prostitute. Play something sweet. Sing plenty of songs so people remember you.”
After seventy years the LORD will visit Tyre. She'll go back to earning her wages and selling herself to every kingdom on earth.
Her goods and her wages will be set apart for the LORD. They won't be hoarded or stored away. They'll go to people who live in the LORD's presence, so they have enough to eat and clothes that last.
Look, the LORD is emptying the earth and laying it waste. He's turning it upside down and scattering the people who live on it.

The same thing will happen to ordinary people and priests, servants and masters, servant girls and mistresses, buyers and sellers, lenders and borrowers, those who charge interest and those who pay it.
The earth will be emptied out and left completely ruined. The LORD has spoken this word.
The earth grieves and withers. The world weakens and fades. Even the people who thought they stood high above everyone else waste away.
The people who live on the earth have polluted it. They crossed the lines of the law, broke the statutes, and tore up the covenant that was meant to last forever.
That's why the curse has eaten up the earth, and the people living on it are found guilty. That's why they're burned up and so few are left.
The new wine mourns. The vines shrivel. Everybody who used to be cheerful lets out a sigh.
The tambourines go quiet. The sound of people celebrating comes to an end. The harp has no more joy to play.
Nobody's singing with their wine. Strong drink tastes bitter to the people who drink it.
The city is broken down and in chaos. Every house is shut tight. Nobody can get in.
People cry out in the streets for wine. Every bit of joy has gone dark. The land's laughter is gone.
The city is left empty and wrecked, and its gate has been smashed.
That's how it'll be among the peoples of the earth, like an olive tree after it's been shaken or a vineyard with only scraps left after harvest.
Those who remain will raise their voices. They'll shout over the LORD's majesty, calling out from the sea.
So give glory to the LORD in the east! Give glory to the name of the LORD, Israel's God, on the islands of the sea!

From the far ends of the earth we hear songs, “Glory to the righteous!” But I said, “I'm wasting away! I'm wasting away! Trouble for me!” The traitors have betrayed us. They've gone all in on betrayal.
Terror, a pit, and a snare are waiting for you, people of the earth.
Run from the sound that terrifies you and you'll fall into the pit. Climb out of the pit and you'll get caught in the snare. The windows above have opened, and the earth's foundations shake.
The earth cracks wide open. The earth is torn apart. The earth shakes violently.
The earth will stagger like somebody drunk and swing back and forth like a hammock. Its rebellion will weigh it down, and it'll fall and never get back up.
That day the LORD will punish the army of the powers up high and the kings down on the earth.
They'll be rounded up like prisoners in a pit and locked up. Many days later, they'll be dealt with.
Then the moon will be embarrassed and the sun ashamed. The LORD of Armies will reign on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem, and his glory will be right there before his elders.
LORD, you're my God. I'll lift you high and praise your name! You've done amazing things you planned long ago, and you've been faithful and true through it all.
You turned a city into rubble, a fortified city into ruins. The palace of foreigners isn't a city anymore. It'll never be rebuilt.
That's why strong peoples will give you glory, and cities of fearsome nations will stand in awe of you.
You've been a fortress for the poor and a safe place for people in trouble. When ruthless people hit like a storm against a wall, you were a shelter from that storm and shade from the heat.
You'll quiet the roar of foreigners like heat dying down in a dry land. Like a cloud taking the heat away, you'll hush the song of ruthless people.
On this mountain the LORD of Armies will throw a feast for all peoples, with the best meat, rich with marrow, and the best wine, aged and strained clear.
On this mountain he'll tear away the covering thrown over every people, the veil spread across all nations.
He's swallowed up death forever! The Lord GOD will wipe the tears from every face and take away his people's shame from the whole earth. The LORD has spoken.
That day people will say, “Look, this is our God! We waited for him, and he'll save us! This is the LORD we waited for. Let's celebrate and be glad that he saves us!”
The LORD's hand will rest on this mountain. Moab will be trampled where he stands, like straw stomped into the watery muck of a manure heap.
He'll stretch his hands out in the middle of it like a swimmer trying to swim, but his pride and all the skill in his hands will be brought low.
He's brought your high fortress walls down, right to the ground, all the way to dust.
That day people in Judah will sing this song: “We've got a strong city. God makes salvation our walls and our defenses.
Open the gates so the nation that does right can come in, the one that stays faithful.
You keep people in perfect peace when their minds stay steady because they trust you.
Put your trust in the LORD forever. The LORD, the LORD is a rock that lasts forever.
He brought down those who live up high, that city that towered over everyone. He lays it low, flat on the ground, right down into the dust.
Feet will walk all over it, the feet of the poor and the footsteps of those in need.”
People who do right walk a straight road. You who are upright make their path level.
Yes, LORD, we've waited for you on the road of your justice. Your name and your reputation are what our souls want.
My soul longs for you at night. Deep inside I reach for you with my whole spirit. When your judgments come on earth, the people of the world learn to do right.
Show kindness to the wicked and they still won't learn what's right. Even in a land of honest people they'll do wrong and miss the LORD's majesty.
LORD, your hand is raised and they don't see it. They'll see your zeal for your people and be put to shame. Fire will eat up your enemies.
LORD, you'll establish peace for us. Everything we've accomplished, you've done for us.
LORD our God, other masters have ruled us besides you. Your name is the only one we'll honor.
Those dead rulers won't live again. Their spirits won't rise. You came against them, destroyed them, and wiped away every memory of them.
You've made the nation bigger, LORD. You've made the nation bigger! You get the glory. You've pushed every border of the land outward.
LORD, they came to you when they were in trouble. They poured out a prayer when your discipline was on them.
Like a pregnant woman whose time has come, crying out through the pain of labor, that's how we've been in front of you, LORD.
We were pregnant, we went through the pain, and all we gave birth to was wind. We haven't brought rescue to the earth, and the people of the world haven't fallen.
Your dead will live! Their bodies will get up. Wake up and sing, you who live in the dust! Your dew is like dew on fresh plants, and the earth will give up the spirits of the dead.
Come on, my people. Go into your rooms and shut the doors behind you. Hide for a little while till the anger passes.
Look, the LORD is coming out from his place to punish the people of the earth for their wrongdoing. The earth will uncover the blood spilled on it and won't hide its dead anymore.
That day the LORD will take his hard, great, powerful sword and punish Leviathan, the fleeing snake, Leviathan, the twisting snake. He'll kill the dragon in the sea.
That day, sing about her: “What a lovely vineyard!
I'm the LORD, and I take care of it. I water it constantly and guard it day and night so nobody can hurt it.
I'm not angry. But if briers and thorns showed up, I'd go to battle! I'd march over them and burn them all together.
Or let them grab hold of my strength and make peace with me. Let them make peace with me.”
In the days ahead, Jacob will take root. Israel will bud and bloom, and they'll cover the world with fruit.
Did the LORD hit Israel as hard as he hit those who attacked them? Were they killed the way their killers were killed?
You dealt with them in measure when you sent them away. You swept them off with a rough blast on the day the east wind blew.

That's how Jacob's guilt will be forgiven. Here's the full result of his sin being taken away. He'll smash every altar stone to bits like chalk, and the Asherah poles and incense altars will never stand again.
The fortified city stands alone. The place where people used to live is empty and deserted like the wilderness. Calves will graze there and lie down there, chewing through its branches.

When the branches dry out, they'll snap off. Women will come and use them for firewood. These people have no understanding, so the one who made them won't have compassion on them, and the one who shaped them won't show them favor.
That day the LORD will thresh from the flowing Euphrates to the brook of Egypt. People of Israel, you'll be gathered up one by one.
That day a great trumpet will blow. Those about to perish in Assyria and those driven out into Egypt will come and worship the LORD on the holy mountain in Jerusalem.
Trouble for the crown the drunkards of Ephraim are so proud of! That gorgeous flower is wilting up above the rich valley where people are overcome with wine.
Look, the Lord has someone mighty and strong. Like a hailstorm that wrecks everything, like floodwaters spilling over, he'll throw them to the ground with his hand.
The crown the drunkards of Ephraim are so proud of will be trampled underfoot.
That fading flower of beauty above the rich valley will be like the first ripe fig before summer. Somebody spots it, picks it, and eats it on the spot.
That day the LORD of Armies will be a glorious crown and a beautiful headpiece for the people he has left.
He'll be a spirit of justice for the person who sits to judge, and strength for those who push the battle back at the gate.

These people reel from wine and stumble from strong drink too. Priest and prophet reel from liquor. The wine has swallowed them. They stumble from strong drink, get their visions wrong, and trip over their own judgments.
Every table is covered in filthy vomit. There's no clean spot anywhere.
“Who does he think he's teaching? Who's he explaining his message to? Babies just taken off the breast, just weaned from milk?
It's rule on rule, rule on rule, line on line, line on line, a little here, a little there.”
So he'll speak to this nation through stumbling lips and another language.
He had told them, “Here's where you can rest. Let the tired ones rest. Here's where you can get your strength back.” They still wouldn't listen.
So the LORD's word to them will be rule on rule, rule on rule, line on line, line on line, a little here, a little there. They'll go, fall backward, break, get trapped, and be taken.
So hear the LORD's word, you mockers ruling these people in Jerusalem.
You've said, “We've made a deal with death and come to terms with the grave. When that flood of punishment sweeps through, it won't reach us. We've made lies our shelter and hidden behind falsehood.”
So the Lord GOD says, “Look, I'm laying a foundation stone in Zion, a stone that's been tested, a precious cornerstone for a foundation you can count on. Whoever believes won't rush in a panic.
I'll use justice as the measuring line and righteousness as the plumb line. Hail will sweep away your shelter of lies. The flood will wash over your hiding place.
Your deal with death will be canceled. Your agreement with the grave won't hold. When the flood of punishment sweeps through, it'll trample you.
Every time it passes through, it'll grab you. It'll come morning after morning, by day and by night. Just understanding the message will be pure terror.”
The bed's too short for you to stretch out, and the blanket's too narrow to wrap around you.
The LORD will rise like he did on Mount Perazim, and he'll be angry like he was in the valley of Gibeon, to do his work, his strange work, and carry out his act, his extraordinary act.
So quit mocking, or your chains will get tighter. I've heard the Lord, GOD of Armies, decree destruction over the whole earth.
Lean in and hear my voice! Listen to what I'm saying!
Does a farmer plow forever before planting? Do they just keep turning dirt over and breaking up clumps?
Once the ground is level, don't they plant dill, scatter cumin seed, put wheat into rows, and plant barley and spelt where each belongs?
Their God teaches them what to do and gives them good judgment.
You don't thresh dill with a sharp tool or roll a cartwheel over cumin. You beat dill out with a stick and cumin with a rod.
Grain has to be ground for bread, so a farmer doesn't thresh it forever. The threshing cart's wheel goes over it, but the horses don't grind it.
This too comes from the LORD of Armies. His advice is wonderful, and his wisdom is excellent.
Trouble for Ariel! Ariel, the city where David camped! Let the years pile up and the feasts come around again.
Then I'll bring trouble on Ariel. There'll be mourning and crying, and she'll be like an altar hearth to me.
I'll camp all around you, post troops to lay siege to you, and build siegeworks against you.
You'll be brought down so low you'll speak from the ground. Your words will mumble out of the dust. Your voice will sound like a spirit speaking from the ground, your words a whisper from the dirt.
But the crowd of your enemies will become like fine dust, and those ruthless people like husks that blow away. It'll happen in a flash, without warning.
The LORD of Armies will come to her with thunder, an earthquake, a huge roar, a whirlwind and storm, and flames of fire that eat everything up.
All those nations fighting Ariel, everyone attacking her and her fortress and crowding in on her, will be like a dream that comes in the night.

It's like a hungry person dreaming they're eating, then waking up still hungry. Or like a thirsty person dreaming they're drinking, then waking up weak and still thirsty. That's how it'll be for all the nations going up against Mount Zion.
Stop and be stunned! Blind yourselves and stay blind! They're drunk, but wine didn't do it. They're staggering, but strong drink didn't do it.
The LORD has poured a spirit of deep sleep over you. He's closed your eyes, the prophets, and covered your heads, the seers.
Every vision has become like words in a sealed book. Hand it to somebody who can read and say, “Read this, please,” and they'll say, “I can't. It's sealed.”
Hand the book to somebody who never learned to read and say, “Read this, please,” and they'll say, “I can't read.”

The Lord said, “These people come close with their mouths and honor me with their lips, but they've moved their hearts far away from me. The reverence they show me is just a rule somebody taught them.

So look, I'll do something amazing among these people, something that will leave them wondering. What their wise people call wisdom will disappear, and the understanding of their clever people will be hidden.”
Trouble for those who bury their plans deep to hide them from the LORD. They do things in the dark and say, “Who's watching us? Who knows what we're doing?”

You've got everything backward! Is a potter just the same as clay? Can a thing someone made say of its maker, “You didn't make me”? Can something shaped say of the one who shaped it, “You don't know what you're doing”?
Won't it be just a little while before Lebanon turns into a fruitful field and that field looks like a forest?
That day deaf people will hear the words of the book, and blind people will see out of the gloom and darkness.
Humble people will find even more joy in the LORD, and the poorest will celebrate the Holy One of Israel.
The ruthless will come to nothing. The mocker will be gone. Everyone watching for a chance to do evil will be cut off,
the people who get someone charged on a word, set traps for the one who corrects them at the gate, and twist testimony to cheat the innocent out of justice.
So the LORD, who redeemed Abraham, says about Jacob's family, “Jacob won't be ashamed anymore, and his face won't go pale.
When he sees his children among him, the work of my hands, they'll honor my name as holy. They'll honor the Holy One of Jacob and stand in awe of the God of Israel.
People whose spirits wandered off will come to understand, and the ones who grumble will take instruction.”
“Trouble for my rebellious children,” says the LORD. “They make plans without me and make deals without my Spirit, piling sin on top of sin.
They head down to Egypt without asking me what to do. They want Pharaoh's power to back them up and Egypt's shadow to keep them safe.
But Pharaoh's power will bring you shame, and hiding in Egypt's shadow will leave you humiliated.
Your officials have reached Zoan, and your messengers have made it to Hanes.
You'll all be ashamed because the people you counted on can't do you any good. They won't help you or get you ahead. They'll only bring shame and disgrace.”

This is the message about the animals of the South. Through a land of trouble and pain, with lions and lionesses, vipers and fiery flying snakes, they haul their riches on young donkeys and their treasures on camels' humps to people who can't help them.
Egypt's help is useless. It gets nothing done. That's why I call her Rahab Who Sits Still.
Now go write this where they can see it, on a tablet. Write it down in a book so it'll be there in the days to come, forever.
These people are rebels, children who lie, children who won't listen to what the LORD teaches.
They tell seers, “Stop seeing!” They tell prophets, “Quit telling us what's right. Tell us something nice. Give us a prophecy we can enjoy, even if it's a lie.
Get off the road and out of our way. Stop putting the Holy One of Israel in front of us.”
So the Holy One of Israel says, “You look down on this word and put your trust in oppression and crooked dealing. That's what you lean on.
So this wrongdoing will be like a crack bulging out of a high wall. It'll give way in an instant and come crashing down.
He'll smash it like a clay pot, break it without holding back. There won't be a piece big enough to scoop a hot coal out of the hearth or dip water out of a cistern.”
The Lord GOD, the Holy One of Israel, said, “Turn back and rest, and you'll be saved. Your strength will be in staying quiet and trusting me.” But you refused.
You said, “No, we'll escape on horses.” So you'll run. You said, “We'll ride on fast horses.” So the ones coming after you will be fast.
A thousand of you will run from one person's threat. At the threat of five you'll all run till you're left like a lone signal pole on a mountaintop, like a banner on a hill.
So the LORD waits to show you grace. He'll rise up to show you mercy, because the LORD is a God of justice. Blessed are all who wait for him.
People will live in Zion, in Jerusalem. You won't cry anymore. He'll show you grace when you cry out. As soon as he hears you, he'll answer.
The Lord may feed you the bread of hardship and give you the water of suffering, but your teachers won't stay hidden. You'll see them with your own eyes.
Turn right or turn left and you'll hear a voice behind you say, “This is the road. Walk on it.”
You'll make the silver coating on your carved idols and the gold plating on your cast idols unclean. You'll toss them away like something filthy and say, “Get out of here!”
He'll send rain for the seed you plant in the ground. The land will produce rich, plentiful food. That day your livestock will graze in wide pastures.
The oxen and young donkeys that plow the ground will eat tasty feed that's been sifted with shovel and fork.
Streams and brooks will run on every high mountain and hill on the day of the big slaughter, when the towers fall.

The moon will shine like the sun, and the sun will shine seven times brighter, like seven days of light all at once, when the LORD wraps up his people's broken bones and heals the wound they were struck with.
Look, the LORD's name comes from far away, burning with anger, with thick smoke rising. His lips are full of fury, and his tongue is like fire that eats everything up.
His breath is like a flood up to the neck. He'll shake the nations through a sieve of destruction and put a bridle in their mouths that leads them to ruin.
You'll sing like you do at night when you keep a holy feast. Your hearts will be glad like someone playing a flute on the way to the LORD's mountain, to Israel's Rock.
The LORD will make his glorious voice heard and show his arm coming down in fierce anger, with flames that devour, a blast, a storm, and hailstones.
The LORD's voice will terrify Assyria. He'll strike it with his rod.
Every blow the LORD lands with his rod of punishment will come with tambourines and harps. He'll fight them with weapons raised.

The place for burning has been ready for a long time. It's prepared for the king. The LORD made the fire pit deep and wide, with fire and plenty of wood. His breath sets it ablaze like a stream of sulfur.

Trouble for people who go down to Egypt for help. They lean on horses, count on chariots because there are so many, and trust horsemen because they're so strong. They don't look to the Holy One of Israel or seek the LORD.
But he's wise too. He'll bring disaster and won't take back a word. He'll rise against the house of evildoers and the people who help them do wrong.

The Egyptians are human. They're no gods. Their horses are flesh and blood, without the power of spirit. When the LORD reaches out his hand, the helper will trip and the one being helped will fall. They'll all be wiped out together.

The LORD told me, “A lion, even a young lion, growls over its prey. Call a whole crowd of shepherds against it and their yelling won't scare it or make it back down. That's how the LORD of Armies will come down to fight on Mount Zion and its heights.
Like birds hovering overhead, the LORD of Armies will guard Jerusalem. He'll guard and rescue it, pass over it and keep it safe.”
People of Israel, come back to the one you turned so far away from.
That day everyone will throw away their silver and gold idols. Your own hands made that sin for you.
“Assyria will fall by a sword no human swings. A sword that doesn't come from people will devour it. Assyria will run from the sword, and its young men will be forced to work.
Its rock will give way in terror, and its rulers will panic at the banner,” says the LORD, whose fire is in Zion and whose furnace is in Jerusalem.
Look, a king will rule by doing what's right, and his officials will govern with justice.
Each will be like a place to hide from the wind and take cover from a storm, like streams running through dry ground, like the shade of a huge rock in an exhausted land.
People who can see won't have their eyes clouded over. People who can hear will pay attention.
People who rush into things will learn to understand. People who stumble over their words will be ready to speak clearly.
Nobody will call a fool noble anymore or treat a crook like somebody worth looking up to.
A fool talks nonsense and plans wrongdoing inside, doing what dishonors God and saying false things about the LORD. They leave hungry people empty and take water away from people who are thirsty.
A crook's ways are evil. They plan to ruin humble people with lies, even when the one in need tells the truth.
But someone noble plans good things and keeps doing them.
Get up, you women taking it easy! Listen to my voice! You daughters who think you've got nothing to worry about, hear what I'm saying!
