In a little more than a year, you carefree women will be shaken. The grapes will fail. There won't be a harvest.
Shake, you women taking it easy! Get upset, you who felt so secure. Take your clothes off and wrap sackcloth around your waists.
Beat your breasts for those lovely fields and the vines that used to bear fruit.
Thorns and briers will come up all over my people's land, even over the houses where people used to celebrate in that joyful city.
The palace will be abandoned. The crowded city will empty out. The hill and the watchtower will become dens for good, a playground for wild donkeys and a pasture for flocks,
until the Spirit is poured on us from above, and the wilderness turns into a fruitful field, and the field grows so thick it's counted as a forest.
Then justice will live in the wilderness, and righteousness will stay in the fruitful field.
Doing what's right will bring peace. The result of righteousness will be quiet and confidence that last forever.
My people will live in peaceful homes, in safe places, and in quiet places to rest,
even if hail flattens the forest and the city is leveled.
Blessed are you who plant beside every stream and let your ox and donkey roam free.

Trouble for you who wrecked other people without getting wrecked, who betrayed people without getting betrayed! When you're done destroying, you'll be destroyed. When you're done betraying, you'll be betrayed.
LORD, show us grace. We've been waiting for you. Be our strength every morning and save us when trouble comes.
At the roar of thunder, the peoples run. When you rise up, the nations scatter.
What you took will be gathered up the way caterpillars gather. People will jump on it like locusts.
The LORD is lifted high because he lives up high. He's filled Zion with justice and righteousness.
Your times will have a solid footing, with plenty of salvation, wisdom, and knowledge. Your treasure is standing in awe of the LORD.
Look, their bravest men are crying outside. The messengers sent to make peace are weeping hard.
The highways are empty. Travelers have stopped coming. He's broken the agreement, treated cities with contempt, and shown no respect for anybody.
The land mourns and wastes away. Lebanon is humiliated and drying up. Sharon looks like a desert, and Bashan and Carmel have been stripped bare.
“Now I'll get up,” says the LORD. “Now I'll rise high. Now I'll be lifted up.
You'll get pregnant with husks and give birth to stubble. Your own breath is the fire that'll eat you up.
The peoples will burn like stone in a lime kiln, like thorns cut down and tossed in the fire.
You who are far away, hear what I've done. You who are close, recognize my strength.”
Sinners in Zion are terrified. The godless can't stop shaking. “Who among us can live with a fire that eats everything up? Who can live with flames that never go out?”
The person who does what's right and speaks honestly, who wants no profit from oppressing people, waves away a bribe, blocks their ears to talk of bloodshed, and shuts their eyes to evil,
will live up high with a fortress of rock to defend them. They'll have bread to eat and water they can count on.
You'll see the king in all his beauty with your own eyes. You'll see a land stretching far away.
You'll think back on the terror. Where's the one who counted? Where's the one who weighed everything? Where's the one who counted the towers?
You won't see those fierce people again, the people whose speech is too hard to follow, whose strange language you can't understand.
Look at Zion, the city where we keep our appointed feasts. You'll see Jerusalem, a peaceful home, a tent that won't be moved. Its stakes will never be pulled out, and none of its ropes will snap.
There the LORD will be with us in his majesty, like a place with wide rivers and streams where no warship with oars and no grand ship will pass.
The LORD is our judge. The LORD gives us our laws. The LORD is our king. He'll save us.
Your ropes hang loose. Nobody could hold the mast steady at its base or spread the sail. Then all that plunder was divided up. Even people who couldn't walk well got a share.
Nobody who lives there will say, “I'm sick.” The people there will be forgiven for what they've done wrong.
Come close and hear this, you nations! Listen, all you peoples! Let the earth and everything in it hear, the whole world and everything it brings forth.
The LORD is furious with every nation and angry with every army. He has marked them for total destruction and handed them over to be slaughtered.
The dead will be thrown out. The smell of their bodies will rise, and the mountains will melt in their blood.
The whole army of the sky will dissolve. The sky will roll up like a scroll, and all its armies will fall away like leaves dropping off a vine or a fig tree.
“My sword has drunk its fill in the sky. Look, it's coming down on Edom, on the people under my curse, to bring judgment.”
The LORD's sword is soaked with blood and covered in fat, the blood of lambs and goats, the fat from rams' kidneys. The LORD has a sacrifice in Bozrah and a great slaughter in the land of Edom.
The wild oxen will fall with them, young bulls along with the strongest bulls. Their land will be drenched with blood, and their dust slick with fat.
The LORD has set a day to take vengeance, a year to settle accounts for Zion.
Edom's streams will turn into pitch and its dust into sulfur. The whole land will be burning pitch.
It won't go out day or night. Its smoke will rise forever. It'll lie in ruins generation after generation, and nobody will ever pass through it.
Pelicans and porcupines will take over. Owls and ravens will live there. He'll stretch the measuring line of chaos across it and drop the plumb line of emptiness.
They'll call for nobles to take charge of the kingdom, but none will be there. All its rulers will come to nothing.
Thorns will sprout in the palaces, nettles and thistles in the fortresses. Jackals will make their home there, and ostriches will roam its courtyards.
Desert animals will meet wolves there, and wild goats will call to each other. Even the night creature will settle there and find a place to rest.
The arrow snake will nest there, lay and hatch her eggs, and gather her young in her shade. The kites will gather there too, each with its mate.
Look it up in the LORD's book and read it. None of these creatures will be missing, and none will be without its mate. His mouth gave the command, and his Spirit gathered them.
He drew the lot for them and measured out their land with his own hand. They'll own it forever and live there generation after generation.
The wilderness and dry ground will be glad. The desert will celebrate and bloom like a rose.
It'll burst into flower, shouting and singing for joy. It'll get the glory of Lebanon and the beauty of Carmel and Sharon. They'll see the LORD's glory, the splendor of our God.
Put strength back into weak hands. Steady those shaky knees.
Tell people with scared hearts, “Be strong! Don't be afraid! Look, your God is coming to take vengeance and set things right. He's coming to save you.”
Then blind eyes will open, and deaf ears will hear.
Then people who couldn't walk will jump like deer, and those who couldn't speak will sing. Water will burst out in the wilderness and streams will run through the desert.
Burning sand will turn into a pool and thirsty ground into springs. Where jackals used to lie down, grass, reeds, and rushes will grow.
A highway will run through there called the Holy Way. People who are unclean won't cross it. It'll be for those who walk the Way, and wicked fools won't go there.
No lion will be on it, and no hungry predator will come up onto it. They won't be found there. The people God redeemed will walk there.
The people the LORD has bought back will return to Zion singing. Joy that lasts forever will be on their heads. They'll find gladness and joy, and sorrow and sighing will run away.
In King Hezekiah's fourteenth year, King Sennacherib of Assyria attacked every fortified city in Judah and took them.
The king of Assyria sent Rabshakeh and a huge army from Lachish to King Hezekiah in Jerusalem. Rabshakeh stood by the water channel from the upper pool, on the road to the cloth washer's field.
Eliakim, Hilkiah's son and the man in charge of the household, came out to meet him, along with Shebna the scribe and Joah the recorder, Asaph's son.
Rabshakeh told them, “Tell Hezekiah this: ‘The great king, the king of Assyria, says, “What are you counting on?
I say your plans and strength for battle are just empty talk. Who are you trusting enough to rebel against me?
Look at Egypt, that cracked reed you're using as a walking stick. Lean on it and it'll go straight through your hand. That's what Pharaoh, king of Egypt, is like for anyone who trusts him.
You might tell me, ‘We trust the LORD our God.’ But isn't he the one whose high places and altars Hezekiah tore down when he told Judah and Jerusalem, ‘You have to worship at this altar’?”
So come on, make a deal with my master, the king of Assyria. I'll give you two thousand horses if you can find enough riders to put on them.
How are you supposed to turn back even one captain among the least of my master's servants? And you're counting on Egypt for chariots and horsemen?
You think I came up to destroy this land without the LORD? The LORD himself told me, “Go up against this land and destroy it.”’”
Eliakim, Shebna, and Joah said, “Please speak to us, your servants, in Aramaic. We understand it. Don't use the language of Judah with the people on the wall listening.”

Rabshakeh said, “Did my master send me with this message just for your master and you? It's for the men sitting on the wall too. They'll be eating their own dung and drinking their own urine right along with you.”
Then he stood and shouted in the language of Judah, “Hear the words of the great king, the king of Assyria!
The king says, ‘Don't let Hezekiah fool you. He can't save you.
Don't let Hezekiah talk you into trusting the LORD by saying, “The LORD will save us for sure. The king of Assyria won't get this city.”’
Don't listen to Hezekiah. The king of Assyria says, ‘Make peace with me and come out to me. Then every one of you can eat from your own vine and fig tree and drink from your own cistern,
until I come to take you to a land like yours, a land with grain and new wine, bread and vineyards.
Watch out for Hezekiah talking you into believing, “The LORD will save us.” Have any of the nations' gods saved their lands from the king of Assyria?
Where are the gods of Hamath and Arpad? Where are the gods of Sepharvaim? Did they save Samaria from me?
Which god of any of these countries saved their land from my hand? So why would the LORD save Jerusalem from my hand?’”
They stayed quiet and didn't say a word back. The king had ordered, “Don't answer him.”

Eliakim, Hilkiah's son and the man in charge of the household, came back to Hezekiah with Shebna the scribe and Joah the recorder, Asaph's son. Their clothes were torn, and they told Hezekiah what Rabshakeh had said.
When King Hezekiah heard what had happened, he tore his clothes, wrapped himself in sackcloth, and went into the LORD's house.
He sent Eliakim, who ran the household, Shebna the scribe, and the senior priests to Isaiah the prophet, Amoz's son. They all wore sackcloth.
They told him, “Hezekiah says, ‘Today we're in trouble. We're being rebuked and rejected. It's like the babies are ready to be born, but there's no strength left to deliver them.

Maybe the LORD your God will hear what Rabshakeh said. His master, the king of Assyria, sent him to throw insults at the living God. Maybe the LORD your God will call him to account for what he's heard. So pray for the few of us who are left.’”
That's how King Hezekiah's servants came to Isaiah.
Isaiah told them, “Tell your master, ‘The LORD says, “Don't be scared of what you heard. The king of Assyria's servants were insulting me with those words.
Look, I'll put a spirit in him. He'll hear news and go back to his own land, and I'll make him fall by the sword there.”’”
Rabshakeh went back and found the king of Assyria fighting Libnah. He'd heard the king had left Lachish.
The king heard news about Tirhakah, king of Ethiopia: “He's come out to fight you.” When he heard that, he sent messengers to Hezekiah.
“Tell Hezekiah king of Judah, ‘Don't let the God you trust fool you by saying, “Jerusalem won't be handed over to the king of Assyria.”
You've heard what Assyria's kings have done to all those lands. They wiped them out. You think you'll get away?
Did the gods of the nations my ancestors destroyed save them? What about Gozan, Haran, Rezeph, and the people of Eden in Telassar?
Where's the king of Hamath, the king of Arpad, the king of Sepharvaim, or the kings of Hena and Ivvah?’”
Hezekiah took the letter from the messengers and read it. Then he went up to the LORD's house and spread the letter out in front of the LORD.
Hezekiah prayed to the LORD.
“LORD of Armies, God of Israel, you sit enthroned among the cherubim. You alone are God over all the kingdoms of the earth. You made heaven and earth.
Lean in and listen, LORD. Open your eyes and look. Hear everything Sennacherib sent to say against the living God.
It's true, LORD. The kings of Assyria have destroyed all those nations and their lands.
They threw their gods into the fire. Those were no gods, just wood and stone made by human hands. That's how they could destroy them.
So now, LORD our God, save us from his hand. Let all the kingdoms on earth know that you alone are the LORD.”
Then Isaiah, Amoz's son, sent Hezekiah this message. “The LORD, Israel's God, says, ‘You've prayed to me about Sennacherib, king of Assyria.
Here's what the LORD has said about him. The virgin daughter of Zion looks down on you and laughs. Daughter Jerusalem shakes her head at you.
Who were you defying and insulting? Who did you raise your voice at and look down on so proudly? The Holy One of Israel.

You sent your servants to defy the Lord, saying, “With all my chariots I've climbed the highest mountains and reached deep into Lebanon. I'll cut down its tallest cedars and its finest cypresses. I'll go to its farthest heights, into the forest of its fertile land.
I dug wells and drank the water, and I'll dry up every river in Egypt with the soles of my feet.”
Haven't you heard? I did this long ago. I planned it in ancient times. Now I've brought it about, so you'd turn those fortified cities into heaps of rubble.
That's why the people there had no strength. They were scared and humiliated. They were like grass in a field, like green shoots, like grass on the roof or a field before the crop comes up.
But I know when you sit down, when you go out and come in, and how you rage against me.
Your rage and arrogance have reached my ears. So I'll put my hook in your nose and my bridle between your lips and turn you back the way you came.
Here's your sign, Hezekiah. This year you'll eat what grows on its own. The next year you'll eat what grows from that. In the third year, plant and harvest. Plant vineyards and eat their fruit.
The survivors of Judah's household will put roots down again and grow fruit up above.
A remnant will come out of Jerusalem, and survivors will escape from Mount Zion. The LORD of Armies will make it happen with his own zeal.’
So here's what the LORD says about the king of Assyria. ‘He won't enter this city or shoot an arrow into it. He won't come up against it with a shield or build a siege mound against it.
He'll go back the way he came. He won't enter this city,’ says the LORD.
‘I'll defend this city and save it for my own sake and for my servant David's sake.’”
Then the LORD's angel went out and struck down 185,000 men in the Assyrian camp. When people got up early in the morning, all they saw were dead bodies.
So Sennacherib, king of Assyria, left, went back to Nineveh, and stayed there.

While he was worshiping in the temple of Nisroch his god, his sons Adrammelech and Sharezer struck him down with the sword. They escaped to the land of Ararat, and his son Esar Haddon became king in his place.
Around then Hezekiah got so sick he was close to death. Isaiah the prophet, Amoz's son, came to him and said, “The LORD says, ‘Get your household in order. You're going to die. You won't recover.’”
Hezekiah turned his face toward the wall and prayed to the LORD.
“Please, LORD, remember how I've lived before you faithfully and with my whole heart. I've done what you see as good.” Then Hezekiah broke down crying.
Then the LORD gave Isaiah a message.
“Go tell Hezekiah, ‘The LORD, the God of your father David, says, “I've heard your prayer and seen your tears. Look, I'm adding fifteen years to your life.
I'll rescue you and this city from the king of Assyria, and I'll defend this city.
Here's the sign from the LORD that he'll do what he just said.
Look, on Ahaz's sundial I'll send the shadow back ten steps from where the sun has taken it.”’” So the sun went back ten steps on the sundial it had gone down.
Here's what King Hezekiah of Judah wrote after he'd been sick and gotten well.
I said, “Right in the middle of my life I'm headed for the gates of the grave. The rest of my years are being taken away.”
I said, “I won't see the LORD, the LORD, in the land of the living. I won't see another person among those who live in this world.
My home is pulled up and carried away like a shepherd's tent. I've rolled up my life the way a weaver rolls up cloth. He'll cut me off the loom. From day to night you're bringing me to an end.
I waited till morning. Like a lion, he crushes all my bones. From day to night you're bringing me to an end.
I chirped like a swallow or a crane and moaned like a dove. My eyes wore out looking up. Lord, I'm being crushed. Stand up for me.”
What can I say? He spoke to me and did it himself. I'll walk carefully for the rest of my years because of the pain my soul went through.
Lord, people live by these things, and in all of them my spirit finds life. You restore me and keep me alive.
Look, I got deep pain in place of peace. But you loved me and pulled my soul out of the pit where things rot. You threw all my sins behind your back.
The grave can't praise you. Death can't celebrate you. People who go down into the pit can't hope for your faithfulness.
The living, yes, the living praise you, like I'm doing today. A father tells his children about your faithfulness.
The LORD will save me. So we'll sing my songs with stringed instruments in the LORD's house all the days we're alive.
Isaiah had said, “Take a cake of figs and put it on the boil as a dressing, and he'll recover.”
Hezekiah had also asked, “What's the sign that I'll go up to the LORD's house?”
About then Merodach-baladan, Baladan's son and king of Babylon, sent Hezekiah letters and a gift. He'd heard Hezekiah had been sick and recovered.

Hezekiah was glad to see the messengers and showed them his treasure house: the silver, the gold, the spices, the precious oil, his whole armory, and everything in his storerooms. He showed them everything in his house and all over his kingdom.
Then Isaiah the prophet came to King Hezekiah and asked, “What did these men say? Where did they come from?” Hezekiah said, “They came from far away, all the way from Babylon.”
Isaiah asked, “What did they see in your house?” Hezekiah answered, “Everything. I showed them every last thing in my treasuries.”
Then Isaiah told Hezekiah, “Hear what the LORD of Armies says.
‘Look, days are coming when everything in your house and everything your ancestors have stored up till now will be hauled off to Babylon. Nothing will be left,’ says the LORD.
‘They'll take away sons who come from you, sons you'll father, and they'll be eunuchs in the king of Babylon's palace.’”
Hezekiah told Isaiah, “The word from the LORD that you've spoken is good.” Then he said, “There'll be peace and faithfulness while I'm alive.”
“Comfort my people. Give them comfort,” says your God.
“Speak gently to Jerusalem. Tell her loud and clear that her fight is over, her guilt is forgiven, and she's received double from the LORD's hand for all her sins.”
A voice is calling, “Clear the LORD's way through the wilderness! Make a straight, level road through the desert for our God.
Raise every valley. Bring every mountain and hill low. Level the uneven ground and turn the rough places into a plain.
Then the LORD's glory will be revealed, and everybody will see it together. The LORD himself has spoken.”
A voice says, “Call out!” Someone asks, “What should I say?” “Everyone is like grass, and all their glory is like a flower out in the field.
Grass dries up and flowers fade when the LORD breathes on them. People really are like grass.
Grass dries up and flowers fade, but our God's word stands forever.”

You with good news for Zion, climb a high mountain. You with good news for Jerusalem, raise your voice with all your strength! Shout it out! Don't be scared! Tell Judah's towns, “Look, here's your God!”
Look, the Lord GOD is coming in power, and his arm rules for him. His reward comes with him, and what he'll give in return goes before him.
He'll feed his flock like a shepherd. He'll scoop the lambs up in his arm and carry them close to his chest. He'll gently guide the ones nursing their young.
Who measured the waters in a cupped hand? Who measured off the sky with the span of a hand, counted the earth's dust in a basket, or weighed the mountains and hills on scales?
Who ever told the LORD's Spirit what to do? Who advised him and taught him anything?
Who did he go to for advice? Who taught him to judge fairly, gave him knowledge, or showed him how to understand?
Look, the nations are a drop in a bucket, a speck of dust on the scales. He picks up the islands like they weigh almost nothing.
All of Lebanon wouldn't give enough wood for the fire, and all its animals wouldn't be enough for a burnt offering.
All the nations are like nothing in front of him. To him they're less than nothing, like a breath that vanishes.
So who are you going to compare God to? What image could possibly look like him?
A craftsperson casts an idol. A goldsmith covers it in gold and makes silver chains for it.
Someone who can't afford that kind of offering picks wood that won't rot and finds a skilled carver to set up an idol that won't topple.
Don't you know? Haven't you heard? Hasn't anyone told you from the beginning? Haven't you understood since the earth's foundations were laid?
He sits above the circle of the earth, and the people on it look like grasshoppers. He stretches the heavens like a curtain and spreads them out like a tent to live in.
He makes rulers count for nothing and makes the judges of the earth meaningless.
They're barely planted, barely sown, barely rooted in the ground. He breathes on them and they dry up, and a whirlwind sweeps them away like stubble.
“So who will you compare me to? Who's my equal?” says the Holy One.
Look up. Who made all these stars? He brings them out like an army, counting them and calling every one by name. He's so mighty and strong that none of them is missing.
Jacob, why do you say this? Israel, why do you keep saying, “The LORD doesn't see what I'm going through. My God is ignoring the justice I'm owed”?
Don't you know? Haven't you heard? The LORD is the everlasting God, the one who made the earth to its farthest ends. He doesn't faint or get tired. Nobody can get to the bottom of his understanding.
He gives power to the weak and builds up the strength of people who have none left.
Even young people get worn out and faint, and young men fall flat.
But people who wait for the LORD will get their strength back. They'll rise on wings like eagles. They'll run without wearing out and walk without fainting. 🦅
“Go quiet before me, you islands. Let the peoples get their strength back. Let them come close and then speak. Let's meet to settle the case.

Who raised someone up from the east? Who called him to his feet in righteousness? He hands nations over to him and puts kings under his rule. He makes them like dust before his sword and stubble blown before his bow.
He chases them and passes through safely, even on roads his feet have never taken before.
Who made it happen and called up generation after generation from the start? I did. I am the LORD, the first, and I'm still the same with the last.”
The islands saw and got scared. The ends of the earth shake. They come closer and gather.
Everyone helps their neighbor and tells their brother, “Stay strong!”

The carpenter gets the goldsmith going. The one smoothing things with a hammer encourages the one striking the anvil. “That joint looks good,” they say, and they nail the idol down so it won't wobble.
“But you, Israel, are my servant. Jacob, I chose you. You're the family of Abraham, my friend.
I took hold of you from the ends of the earth and called you from its farthest corners. I told you, ‘You're my servant. I chose you, and I haven't thrown you away.’
Don't be scared, because I'm with you. Don't panic, because I'm your God. I'll make you strong. I'll help you. I'll hold you up with my righteous right hand.
Look, everyone furious with you will be ashamed and humiliated. The people who fight you will come to nothing and perish.
You'll look for the people who came after you, and you won't find them. Whoever goes to war against you will be like nothing, like they never existed.
I'm the LORD your God. I'll hold your right hand and tell you, ‘Don't be afraid. I'll help you.’
Don't be afraid, Jacob, you little worm, and you people of Israel. I'll help you,” says the LORD. “The Holy One of Israel is the one who redeems you.
Look, I've made you a new threshing tool with sharp teeth. You'll thresh mountains and grind them down, and turn hills into husks.
You'll toss them into the air, and the wind will carry them off. A whirlwind will scatter them. You'll celebrate in the LORD and take pride in the Holy One of Israel.
The poor and needy look for water and can't find any. Their tongues are dry from thirst. I, the LORD, will answer them. I, Israel's God, won't leave them behind.
I'll open up rivers on bare heights and springs in the middle of valleys. I'll turn the wilderness into pools of water and dry land into springs.
I'll plant cedar, acacia, myrtle, and oil trees in the wilderness. I'll put cypress, pine, and box trees together out in the desert.
Then people can see it, know it, think about it, and understand together that the LORD's hand did this. The Holy One of Israel made it happen.
Make your case,” says the LORD. “Bring out your best arguments!” says Jacob's King.
“Let those idols step up and tell us what's going to happen! Tell us what happened before so we can think it through and see where it ended. Or show us what's coming.
Tell us what'll happen from here on so we know you're gods. Go ahead, do something good or something bad. Give us something we can all see and be shaken by.
Look, you're nothing, and your work comes to nothing. Anyone who chooses you is doing something disgusting.
“I raised someone up from the north and he came, someone from where the sun rises who calls on my name. He'll come down on rulers like mortar underfoot, like a potter treading clay.
Who announced this from the start so we could know? Who said it ahead of time so we could say, ‘He was right’? Nobody announced it. Nobody showed us. Nobody heard a word from you.
I was the first to say to Zion, ‘Look, here they are!’ And I'll give Jerusalem someone who brings good news.
I look around and there's nobody. There's no adviser among them who can answer a single word when I ask.
Look at them. All their work is empty and amounts to nothing. Their cast idols are wind and confusion.
“Look at my servant, the one I hold up. I chose him, and my whole heart delights in him. I've put my Spirit on him, and he'll bring justice to the nations.
He won't shout or raise his voice to make himself heard in the street.
He won't snap a bruised reed or put out a wick that's barely burning. He'll faithfully bring justice.
He won't give out or lose heart before he's established justice on earth. The islands wait for his teaching.”

Here's what God the LORD says, the one who made the heavens and stretched them out, who spread out the earth and everything that grows from it, who gives breath to the people on it and spirit to those who walk it.
“I, the LORD, called you in righteousness. I'll hold your hand and keep you safe. I'll make you a covenant for the people and a light for the nations,
to open blind eyes, bring prisoners out of the dungeon, and get people sitting in darkness out of prison.
“I am the LORD. That's my name. I won't give my glory to anyone else or give my praise to carved idols.
Look, what I said before has happened. Now I'm announcing new things. I'll tell you about them before they even come up.”
Sing the LORD a new song! Let his praise ring from the ends of the earth, from you who go down to the sea and everything in it, from the islands and everyone who lives there.
Let the wilderness and its towns raise their voices, along with the villages where Kedar lives. People of Sela, sing! Shout from the mountaintops!
Give the LORD glory and tell the islands what he's worthy of.
The LORD will go out like a mighty warrior and stir up his zeal like someone going to battle. He'll raise a battle cry and shout out loud. He'll defeat his enemies.
“I've been quiet a long time. I kept still and held myself back. Now I'll cry out like someone in labor. I'll gasp and pant.
I'll lay mountains and hills to waste and dry up everything growing on them. I'll turn rivers into islands and dry up the pools.

I'll bring blind people along a road they don't know and lead them on paths they've never taken. I'll turn the darkness ahead of them into light and straighten out the crooked places. I'll do all of that and won't leave them behind.
“People who trust carved images and tell cast idols, ‘You're our gods,’ will be turned back and completely put to shame.
“If you're deaf, listen! If you're blind, look so you can see!
Who's blind like my own servant? Who's as deaf as the messenger I send? Who's as blind as the one at peace with me, as blind as the LORD's servant?
You see plenty and still don't pay attention. His ears are open and he still doesn't listen.
The LORD took pleasure, for the sake of his righteousness, in making his teaching great and honorable.

But these people have been robbed and picked clean. They're all trapped in holes, hidden away in prisons. They've been taken captive, and nobody rescues them. They've become plunder, and nobody says, ‘Give them back!’
Which of you will listen to this? Who'll pay attention now and keep listening for the days ahead?
Who handed Jacob over as plunder and Israel over to robbers? Wasn't it the LORD, the one we sinned against? They refused to walk his paths and disobeyed his teaching.
So he poured out his fierce anger on them and brought the full force of battle. Fire closed in around them, but they didn't understand. It burned them, but they didn't take it to heart.”
But now the LORD who made you, Jacob, the one who shaped you, Israel, says, “Don't be afraid. I've bought you back. I called you by name. You're mine.
When you go through deep water, I'll be with you. When you cross rivers, they won't sweep over you. When you walk through fire, you won't burn, and the flames won't scorch you.
I'm the LORD your God, the Holy One of Israel, the one who saves you. I gave Egypt to get you back, and Ethiopia and Seba in your place.
You're precious to me and I honor you. I love you, so I'll give people in your place and nations in exchange for your life.
Don't be afraid. I'm with you. I'll bring your children from the east and gather you from the west.
I'll tell the north, ‘Give them back!’ and the south, ‘Don't hold them back! Bring my sons from far away and my daughters from the ends of the earth.
Bring everyone who carries my name, everyone I created for my glory, everyone I shaped and made.’”
Bring out the people who have eyes but are blind, and people who have ears but are deaf.

Let all the nations gather and all the peoples come together. Which of them can announce this and show us what happened before? Let them bring witnesses who can prove they're right, or let them listen and say, “That's true.”
“You're my witnesses,” says the LORD, “along with the servant I chose, so you can know me, believe me, and understand that I am he. No god was formed before me, and none will come after me.
I myself am the LORD. There's no one besides me who saves.
I announced it, I saved you, and I showed you what would happen. No foreign god was among you. So you're my witnesses,” says the LORD, “and I am God.
I've been the same since the first day. Nobody can snatch anything out of my hand. When I act, who can stop me?”
The LORD, the one who redeems you, the Holy One of Israel, says, “For your sake I've sent to Babylon, and I'll bring them all down as fugitives, even the Chaldeans in the ships they were so proud of.
I am the LORD, your Holy One, the one who made Israel, your King.”
The LORD makes a road through the sea and a path through the mighty waters.
He brings out the chariots and horses, the army and its mighty warriors. They all lie down together and won't get up. They're snuffed out like a wick. He says,
“Quit looking back to what happened before. Don't keep dwelling on the old days.
Look, I'm doing something new! It's already springing up. Can't you see it? I'll even make a road through the wilderness and rivers in the desert.
Wild animals will honor me, the jackals and the ostriches, because I'll give water in the wilderness and rivers in the desert to give my chosen people something to drink.
I made these people for myself so they'd tell the world my praise.
But you haven't called on me, Jacob. You got tired of me, Israel.
You haven't brought me sheep for burnt offerings or honored me with your sacrifices. I haven't weighed you down with offerings or worn you out asking for frankincense.
You haven't spent money on sweet cane for me or given me my fill of the fat from your sacrifices. You've loaded me down with your sins and worn me out with your wrongdoing.
I am the one who wipes your wrongs away for my own sake. I won't remember your sins.
Remind me. Let's argue it out together. Make your case so you can be shown to be right.
Your first father sinned, and your teachers broke faith with me.
So I'll strip the leaders of the sanctuary of their sacred standing. I'll make Jacob a curse and Israel a name people throw around as an insult.”
Now listen, Jacob, my servant. Israel, you're the one I chose.
The LORD made you and shaped you from the womb. He's the one who'll help you, and he says, “Don't be afraid, Jacob, my servant. Don't be afraid, Jeshurun, the one I chose.
I'll pour water on thirsty people and streams on dry ground. I'll pour my Spirit on your descendants and my blessing on your children.
They'll spring up among the grass like willows growing by the streams.
One will say, ‘I belong to the LORD.’ Another will take Jacob's name. Another will write ‘Belonging to the LORD’ on his hand and honor the name of Israel.”
The LORD, Israel's King and Redeemer, the LORD of Armies, says, “I'm the first and I'm the last. There's no God besides me.
Who's like me? Who can call out and announce what happened and lay it out for me, going back to when I established the people long ago? Let them say what's coming and what will happen.
Don't be afraid or let fear take over. Didn't I tell you long ago and show you what was coming? You're my witnesses. Is there a God besides me? There isn't. I know no other Rock.”
Everyone who carves an idol is wasting their time. Those things they love won't do them any good. Their own witnesses don't see or understand, and they'll end up ashamed.
Who makes a god or casts an image that can't do a thing?
Look, everyone who backs the maker will end up ashamed. The craftspeople are only human. Let them all get together and stand up. They'll be scared and ashamed together.
A blacksmith takes up his ax and works over the coals. He shapes it with hammers and puts his arm into the work. When he gets hungry his strength goes, and if he doesn't drink water he gets faint.

A carpenter stretches out a line and marks the wood with a pencil. He shapes it with planes and marks it with a compass. He makes it look like a person, with all a person's beauty, to sit inside a house.
He cuts cedars for himself and takes cypress and oak. He lets a tree grow strong for him among the trees in the forest. He plants a cypress, and the rain feeds it.
Then it becomes fuel. He takes some to warm himself, burns some to bake bread, and makes a god to worship. He carves an image and bows down to it.
He burns part of the wood in the fire. Over part of it he roasts meat and eats till he's full. He warms up and says, “Ah, that's warm. Look at that fire.”
Out of the rest he makes a god, his carved image. He bows low, worships it, and prays, “Save me, because you're my god!”
They don't know and they don't stop to think. Their eyes have been shut so they can't see, and their hearts so they can't understand.

Nobody thinks it through or knows enough to say, “I burned part of it, baked bread over its coals, and roasted meat and ate it. Am I really going to make something disgusting out of what's left? Am I going to bow down to a tree trunk?”
He's feeding on ashes. His own fooled heart has led him off course. He can't save himself or even ask, “Aren't I holding a lie in my right hand?”
Remember these things, Jacob and Israel. You're my servant. I shaped you, and you serve me. Israel, I won't forget you.
I've wiped your wrongs away like a thick cloud and your sins like mist. Come back to me. I've bought you back.
Sing, heavens, because the LORD has done it! Shout, depths of the earth! Mountains, forests, and every tree, burst into song! The LORD bought Jacob back and will show his glory in Israel.
The LORD, the one who redeems you and shaped you from the womb, says, “I'm the LORD, the one who makes everything. I stretched the heavens out alone and spread the earth out by myself.
I wreck the signs of liars and make fortune-tellers look crazy. I turn wise people around and make what they know look foolish.
I confirm what my servant says and carry out what my messengers announce. I tell Jerusalem, ‘People will live in you again,’ and Judah's towns, ‘You'll be rebuilt. I'll raise up your ruins.’
I say to the deep, ‘Dry up,’ and, ‘I'll dry up your rivers.’
I say about Cyrus, ‘He's my shepherd. He'll do everything I want.’ I say about Jerusalem, ‘She'll be rebuilt,’ and about the temple, ‘Your foundation will be laid.’”
The LORD speaks to Cyrus, the one he anointed. “I've taken your right hand to bring nations down before you and strip kings of their armor, to open doors ahead of you and keep the gates from closing.
I'll go ahead of you and smooth out the rough places. I'll smash bronze doors and cut iron bars apart.
I'll give you treasure kept in the dark and riches hidden away, so you'll know I'm the LORD, Israel's God, the one who calls you by name.
For Jacob my servant and Israel my chosen one, I called you by name and gave you a title even though you didn't know me.
I'm the LORD. There's no one else. There's no God besides me. I'll make you strong even though you haven't known me,
so people from where the sun rises to where it sets will know there's no one besides me. I'm the LORD, and there's no one else.
I shape the light and create darkness. I make peace and bring calamity. I'm the LORD, the one who does all of it.
Heavens, let it rain from above! Skies, pour down righteousness. Let the earth open up and grow salvation, with righteousness springing up alongside it. I, the LORD, created it.

Trouble for anybody who picks a fight with their maker, a clay pot among all the clay pots on the ground! Does clay ask the person shaping it, ‘What are you making?’ Does your work say, ‘You don't even have hands’?
Trouble for the one who asks a father, ‘What kind of child did you father?’ or asks a mother, ‘What did you give birth to?’”
The LORD, the Holy One of Israel and the one who made Israel, says, “You ask me what's coming for my children, and then you try to boss me around about what my hands have made!
I made the earth and created people to live on it. My own hands stretched out the heavens, and I gave orders to all their armies.
I raised him up in righteousness and I'll straighten all his roads. He'll build my city and let my exiles go free without taking payment or a reward,” says the LORD of Armies.

The LORD says, “Egypt's wealth from its work and Ethiopia's goods will come over to you, along with the tall Sabeans. They'll belong to you and follow you, coming over in chains. They'll bow down and plead with you, ‘God really is with you. There's no one else. There is no other god.
You truly are a God who hides himself, God of Israel, the one who saves.’”
They'll all end up ashamed and confused. The people making idols will go off disgraced together.
But the LORD will save Israel with a salvation that lasts forever. You won't be put to shame or left humiliated, ever.
The LORD made the heavens. He's the God who shaped the earth and set it firm. He made it for people to live in and didn't create it to sit empty. He says, “I am the LORD. There is no other.
I didn't speak in secret from some dark corner of the land. I didn't tell Jacob's children, ‘Look for me and you'll get nowhere.’ I, the LORD, speak what's right and declare what's true.
“Gather together, you who've escaped from the nations. Come close. People who haul around wooden idols and pray to a god that can't save them don't know what they're doing.

Say what you've got to say and make your case. Get together and talk it over. Who showed this from ancient times? Who announced it back then? Wasn't it me, the LORD? There is no other God besides me. I'm a just God and a Savior. There's no one besides me.
“Look to me and be saved, all you at the ends of the earth. I am God, and there is no other.
I've sworn by my own name. I've spoken a righteous word and won't take it back. Every knee will bow to me, and every tongue will swear an oath.
They'll say about me, ‘Only in the LORD are righteousness and strength.’” People will come to him, and everyone who raged against him will end up ashamed.
All of Israel's descendants will be made right in the LORD, and they'll celebrate!
Bel bows. Nebo stoops. Animals and livestock have to haul their idols. Those things you carried around are heavy loads on animals already worn out.
Both gods stoop and bow together. They can't rescue the load, and they themselves are carried off into captivity.
“Listen to me, family of Jacob, and everyone left of Israel's family. I've carried you since you were born, held you up since the womb.
Even when you're old, I'll still be the same. Even when your hair goes gray, I'll carry you. I made you. I'll bear you up. I'll carry you and get you out of danger.
“Who are you going to compare me to? Who could you call my equal, like the two of us are the same?
Some people dump gold out of a bag and weigh silver on a scale. They hire a goldsmith to make it into a god. Then they drop to the ground and worship it.
They hoist it onto a shoulder, carry it over, and set it in its spot. That's where it stands. It can't move. Cry out to it and it can't answer. It can't get anyone out of trouble.
“Remember this and stand firm. Bring it back to mind, you rebels.
Remember what happened long ago. I am God, and there isn't another. I am God, and nobody is like me.
I tell the end from the beginning. From ancient times I announce things that haven't happened yet. I say, ‘My plan will stand. I'll do everything I want to do.’
I call a bird of prey from the east, the man who will carry out my plan from far away. I've spoken, and I'll make it happen. I've planned it, and I'll do it.
Listen to me, you stubborn hearts, you who are far from doing what's right.
I'm bringing my righteousness close. It's not far away, and my salvation won't be late. I'll give Zion salvation and Israel my glory.
“Come down and sit in the dust, virgin daughter of Babylon. Sit on the ground with no throne, daughter of the Chaldeans. Nobody will call you tender and delicate anymore.
Take up the millstones and grind flour. Take off your veil, pull up your skirt, bare your legs, and wade through the rivers.
You'll be stripped bare, and everyone will see your shame. I'll take vengeance and won't spare anyone.”
The one who redeems us is the Holy One of Israel. His name is the LORD of Armies.
“Sit quiet and go into the dark, daughter of the Chaldeans. Nobody will call you the queen of kingdoms anymore.
I was angry with my people. I let my inheritance be profaned and handed them over to you. You showed them no mercy. You put an especially heavy load on the elderly.
You said, ‘I'll be a princess forever,’ so you never took any of this to heart or thought about how it would end.
“Now listen, you who live for pleasure and sit there feeling safe. You tell yourself, ‘It's all about me. There's nobody besides me. I'll never be a widow or know what it's like to lose my children.’
Both things will hit you in one moment, on a single day. You'll lose your children and become a widow. They'll hit you with full force despite all your magic and all those spells.
You trusted your wickedness and said, ‘Nobody sees me.’ Your wisdom and knowledge led you crooked. Deep down you said, ‘It's all about me. There's nobody besides me.’
So disaster will come on you, and you won't know when it breaks. Trouble will land on you and you won't be able to get rid of it. Ruin you can't explain will come out of nowhere.
“Go on, stand there with all the spells and magic you've worked at since you were young. See if any of it helps you. See if it lets you win.
You're worn out from all your advisers. Let your astrologers, stargazers, and people who predict the future month by month stand up and save you from what's coming.
Look, they're like dry stubble. Fire will burn them up. They can't save themselves from the flames. This won't be a coal to warm your hands at or a fire to sit beside.
That's what you'll get from everything you worked at. The people who've done business with you since you were young will wander off, each their own way. Nobody will be there to save you.

“Listen to this, family of Jacob, you who go by the name of Israel and came from the waters of Judah. You swear by the LORD's name and talk about Israel's God, but you do it without truth or righteousness.
You call yourselves people of the holy city and say you lean on Israel's God. The LORD of Armies is his name.
I announced what happened before, long before it came. I spoke and made it known. Then I acted suddenly, and it happened.
I knew how stubborn you were, with a neck like an iron tendon and a forehead like bronze.
That's why I told you way back. I showed you before it happened so you couldn't say, ‘My idol did it. My carved image and my cast image gave the orders.’
You heard me. Now look at all of it. Aren't you going to speak up about it? From now on I'm showing you new things, hidden things you've never known.
They're being created now. They aren't from long ago. You hadn't heard about them before today, so you can't say, ‘Yeah, I knew that already.’
You didn't hear it. You didn't know it. Your ear has been closed for ages. I knew how badly you'd betray me, and you've been known as a rebel since the womb.
For my name's sake I'll put off my anger. For the sake of my praise I'll hold it back so I don't cut you off.
Look, I've refined you, though it wasn't like refining silver. I chose you in the furnace of suffering.
For my own sake, for my own sake, I'll do it. Why should I let my name be dragged through the mud? I won't give my glory to someone else.
“Listen to me, Jacob, and you, Israel, the one I called. I am he. I'm the first, and I'm the last.
My hand laid the earth's foundation, and my right hand spread out the heavens. When I call them, they all stand up together.
“Everybody gather and listen! Which of them has announced these things? The one the LORD loves will carry out what he wants against Babylon, and his arm will come against the Chaldeans.
I spoke. I called him and brought him here. He'll succeed on the road he's taking.
“Come close and hear this. ‘From the beginning I haven't spoken in secret. From the moment it happened, I was there.’” Now the Lord GOD has sent me with his Spirit.
The LORD, your Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel, says, “I'm the LORD your God. I teach you what does you good and lead you down the road you should take.
If only you'd listened to my commands! Your peace would've flowed like a river, and your righteousness would've rolled in like waves of the sea.
Your children would've been as many as the sand, your descendants as countless as its grains. Their name would never be cut off or wiped out in front of me.”
Get out of Babylon! Run from the Chaldeans! Announce it with a shout of joy. Tell it all the way to the ends of the earth: “The LORD has bought back Jacob, his servant!”
They weren't thirsty when he led them through the deserts. He made water flow out of a rock for them. He split the rock, and the water gushed out.
“There's no peace for the wicked,” says the LORD.
Listen to me, you islands. Pay attention, you peoples far away. The LORD called me from the womb. Before I was born he spoke my name.
He made my mouth like a sharp sword and hid me in the shadow of his hand. He made me a polished arrow and kept me close in his quiver.
He told me, “You're my servant, Israel. I'll show my glory through you.”
But I said, “I worked for nothing. I used up my strength and got nowhere. Still, the LORD holds the justice I'm owed, and my God holds my reward.”
Now the LORD has spoken, the one who shaped me in the womb to be his servant, to bring Jacob back and gather Israel to him. The LORD honors me, and my God has become my strength.

He says, “Bringing Jacob's tribes back and restoring the people of Israel who survived is too small a job for my servant. I'll also make you a light to the nations so my salvation reaches the ends of the earth.”

The LORD, Israel's Redeemer and Holy One, says this to the one people despise, the one the nation can't stand, the servant of rulers: “Kings will see you and stand up. Rulers will bow down because the LORD is faithful, the Holy One of Israel who chose you.”

The LORD says, “I answered you at the right time and helped you on the day of salvation. I'll keep you safe and make you a covenant for the people, to restore the land and give them back the inheritance that's been left in ruins.
You'll tell prisoners, ‘Come out!’ and people in darkness, ‘Show yourselves!’ They'll feed along the roads, with pasture on every bare hill.
They won't go hungry or thirsty. The heat and sun won't strike them, because the one who has mercy on them will lead them and guide them beside springs of water.
I'll make roads across all my mountains and raise up my highways.
Look, some will come from far away, some from the north and west, and some from the land of Sinim.”
Sing, heavens! Celebrate, earth! Mountains, break out in song! The LORD has comforted his people and will show compassion to those who suffer.
But Zion said, “The LORD left me behind. The Lord forgot me.”
“Can a mother forget the baby she's nursing and have no compassion for the child she carried? Even if she forgets, I won't forget you.
Look, I've engraved you on the palms of my hands. Your walls are always in front of me.
Your children hurry back. The people who wrecked you and left you in ruins are leaving.
Look up and see what's happening all around you. They're gathering and coming to you. As surely as I live,” says the LORD, “you'll wear them like jewelry, like a bride getting dressed up.
“Your ruined places, your empty spaces, the land that was destroyed, will be too small for everyone living there. The people who swallowed you up will be far away.
The children you thought you'd lost will tell you, ‘It's too crowded here. Give me somewhere to live.’
Then you'll ask yourself, ‘Who had all these children for me? I lost my children and was all alone, exiled and wandering from place to place. Who raised them? I was left by myself. Where were they?’”
The Lord GOD says, “Look, I'll lift my hand to the nations and raise my banner for the peoples. They'll carry your sons close to their chests and bring your daughters on their shoulders.

Kings will raise your children and queens will nurse them. They'll bow to you with their faces to the ground and lick the dust at your feet. Then you'll know I'm the LORD, and those who wait for me won't be put to shame.”
Can anyone take loot back from a mighty warrior or rescue captives held under a lawful claim?
But the LORD says, “Even a mighty warrior's captives will be taken back, and what the ruthless stole will be recovered. I'll fight the ones who fight you, and I'll save your children.
I'll make your oppressors eat their own flesh and get drunk on their own blood like sweet wine. Then everyone will know that I, the LORD, am your Savior and Redeemer, the Mighty One of Jacob.”

The LORD says, “Where's the divorce paper I gave your mother when I sent her away? Which of my creditors did I sell you to? Look, your own wrongdoing got you sold, and your rebellion is why your mother was sent away.

Why was nobody there when I came? Why didn't anybody answer when I called? Is my arm too short to buy you back? Have I lost the power to rescue you? Look, one rebuke from me dries up the sea. I turn rivers into dry ground, and their fish stink and die of thirst because there's no water.
I dress the heavens in black and cover them with sackcloth.”
The Lord GOD taught me how to speak so I could give worn-out people words that help them keep going. Morning after morning he wakes me up and opens my ears to listen like a student.
The Lord GOD opened my ear. I didn't rebel or turn back.
I gave my back to the people beating me and my cheeks to those pulling out my beard. I didn't hide my face from shame or spit.
The Lord GOD will help me. That's why I haven't been put to shame. I've set my face hard as flint, and I know I won't end up disgraced.
The one who says I'm in the right is near. Who wants to charge me? Let's stand up together. Who's got a case against me? Let them come close.
Look, the Lord GOD will help me! Who's going to condemn me? They'll all wear out like old clothes and get eaten up by moths.
Who among you stands in awe of the LORD and listens to his servant? If you're walking in the dark without a light, trust the LORD's name and lean on your God.

Look, all of you who start your own fire and surround yourselves with torches, go on and walk in the flames you lit and among the torches you set burning. Here's what you'll get from my hand. You'll lie down in sorrow.
“Listen to me, you who chase after what's right and look for the LORD. Look back at the rock you were cut from and the quarry you came out of.
Look back to Abraham your father and Sarah who gave birth to you. When I called him he was just one man. I blessed him and made him into many.
The LORD has comforted Zion and all her ruined places. He's made her wilderness like Eden and her desert like the LORD's garden. There'll be joy and gladness there, thanks and the sound of singing.
“Listen to me, my people. Hear me, my nation. Teaching will go out from me, and I'll make my justice a light for the peoples.
My righteousness is close. My salvation has gone out, and my arms will judge the peoples. The islands will wait for me and trust my strength.

Look up at the heavens and down at the earth. The heavens will disappear like smoke, and the earth will wear out like clothes. The people who live there will die too, but my salvation will last forever, and my righteousness won't be wiped out.
“Listen to me, you who know what's right, you who carry my teaching in your heart. Don't be scared when people mock you or let their insults shake you.
Moths will eat them up like old clothes, and worms will eat them like wool. My righteousness will last forever, and my salvation for every generation.”
Wake up, wake up, arm of the LORD! Put on your strength! Wake up like in the old days, the generations long ago. Weren't you the one who cut Rahab to pieces and pierced the monster?
Weren't you the one who dried up the sea, the waters of the great deep, and made a road across its depths for the people you redeemed?
Those the LORD bought back will return, singing as they come to Zion. Joy that never ends will crown their heads. Gladness and joy will be theirs, and sorrow and sighing will run away.
“I'm the one who comforts you. Who are you to be scared of people who are going to die, human beings who'll wither like grass?

Have you forgotten the LORD who made you, stretched out the heavens, and laid the earth's foundations? Are you scared all day of the oppressor's rage when he gets ready to destroy? Where's all that rage now?
The prisoner in exile will be set free soon. He won't die and go down into the pit, and his bread won't run out.
I'm the LORD your God, the one who stirs up the sea till its waves roar. The LORD of Armies is my name.
I've put my words in your mouth and covered you in the shadow of my hand, so I can set the heavens in place, lay the earth's foundations, and say to Zion, ‘You're my people.’”
Wake up, wake up! Get on your feet, Jerusalem! You drank the cup of the LORD's anger from his own hand. You drank the bowl that made you stagger and drained it to the last drop.
Of all the sons she gave birth to, there's nobody to guide her. Of all the children she raised, nobody takes her hand.
You've been hit twice. Who's going to grieve with you? Ruin and destruction, hunger and the sword. How can I comfort you?
Your children have collapsed at every street corner like antelopes caught in a net. They've had their fill of the LORD's anger, the rebuke of your God.
So listen to this, you who've been crushed and are staggering like you're drunk, though you haven't had wine.
The Lord GOD, your God who argues the case of his people, says, “Look, I've taken the cup that made you stagger out of your hand, the bowl filled with my anger. You'll never drink from it again.
I'll put it in the hands of the people who crushed you, who told you, ‘Get down so we can walk over you.’ You flattened your back like the ground, like a street for people to walk across.”
Wake up, wake up, Zion! Put your strength on. Jerusalem, holy city, put on your beautiful clothes. From now on the uncircumcised and unclean won't come into you anymore.
Shake the dust off! Get up and take your seat, Jerusalem! Pull the chains off your neck, captive daughter of Zion!
The LORD says, “You were sold for nothing, and you'll be bought back without money.”
The Lord GOD says, “At first my people went down to live in Egypt, and then Assyria oppressed them for no reason.
So what am I doing here,” says the LORD, “when my people have been taken away for nothing? Their rulers mock them, and my name gets dragged through the dirt nonstop,” says the LORD.
“So my people will know my name. That day they'll know I'm the one speaking. Look, it's me.”
How beautiful it is to see those feet coming over the mountains with good news, announcing peace, bringing good news, proclaiming salvation, and telling Zion, “Your God reigns!”
Your watchmen raise their voices and sing together. They'll see it with their own eyes when the LORD comes back to Zion.
You ruins of Jerusalem, come on, sing for joy together! The LORD has comforted his people and bought Jerusalem back.
The LORD has bared his holy arm for all the nations to see. All the ends of the earth have seen our God's salvation.
Go! Get out of there! Don't touch anything unclean. Leave her behind. You who carry the LORD's vessels, clean yourselves up.
You won't have to rush out or flee. The LORD will go ahead of you, and Israel's God will cover you from behind.
Look, my servant will act wisely. He'll be lifted up and honored and raised very high.
So many were shocked when they saw you. His looks were disfigured beyond anyone else's, his form so marred he hardly looked human.
In the same way he'll cleanse many nations. Kings will go quiet in front of him. They'll see what nobody told them and understand what they'd never heard.
Who believed what we told them? Who has seen the LORD's arm revealed?

He grew up before the LORD like a young shoot, like a root out of dry ground. He didn't have looks or majesty that would turn our heads. When we saw him there was nothing beautiful that drew us to him.
People looked down on him and rejected him. He knew suffering and sickness firsthand. We turned our faces away from him like he was nothing, and we gave him no respect.
He really did carry our sickness and bear our pain. We thought God had struck him and brought that suffering on him.
But he was pierced for our rebellion and crushed for the wrong we've done. The punishment that brought us peace fell on him, and his wounds are how we're healed.
All of us have wandered like sheep. Every one of us went our own way, and the LORD put all our wrongdoing on him.
People pushed him down and made him suffer, but he didn't say a word. Like a lamb being led to slaughter, like a sheep quiet in front of the people shearing it, he kept his mouth shut.
He was taken away through oppression and judgment. Who in his generation stopped to think that he was cut off from the land of the living and struck for my people's rebellion?
They assigned him a grave with wicked people, and in his death he was with a rich man. He'd never done violence or told a lie.
Yet the LORD chose to crush him and made him suffer. When his life is made an offering for sin, he'll see his descendants and live long, and what the LORD wants will succeed in his hand.
After all his suffering, he'll see the light and be satisfied. My righteous servant will make many right through knowledge of him, and he'll carry their wrongdoing.

So I'll give him a share with the great, and he'll divide the spoils with the strong. He poured out his life to death and was counted with rebels. Yet he carried the sins of many and pleaded for those who rebelled.

“Sing, you who couldn't have children, you who never gave birth! Break out singing and shout, you who never went through labor. The woman left alone will have more children than the married woman,” says the LORD.
“Make more room for your tent. Stretch your curtains out wide and don't hold back. Lengthen the ropes and drive the stakes in strong.
You'll spread to the right and left. Your children will take possession of nations and settle in cities that were empty.
“Don't be scared. You won't be put to shame. Don't be embarrassed. You won't be disgraced. You'll forget the shame of your youth and won't remember the disgrace of being a widow anymore.
The one who made you is your husband. His name is the LORD of Armies. The Holy One of Israel is the one who redeems you. He'll be called the God of the whole earth.
The LORD called you like a wife who's been left behind and hurt deep down, like the wife of someone's youth who was sent away,” says your God.
“I left you for a little while, but I'll gather you back with great mercy.
In a rush of anger I hid my face from you for a moment. With faithful love that lasts forever, I'll have mercy on you,” says the LORD who redeems you.
“This is like the floodwaters of Noah to me. I swore those waters would never cover the earth again. In the same way I've sworn I won't be angry with you or rebuke you.
Mountains may move and hills may disappear, but my faithful love won't leave you, and my covenant of peace won't be taken away,” says the LORD, who has mercy on you.
“You've suffered, been tossed around by storms, and had nobody to comfort you. Look, I'll set your stones in beautiful colors and lay your foundations with sapphires.
I'll make your towers out of rubies, your gates out of sparkling jewels, and all your walls out of precious stones.
The LORD will teach all your children, and they'll have deep peace.
You'll be set on a foundation of righteousness. Oppression will be far away, and you won't live scared. Terror won't come near you.
People might gather against you, but I won't be the one sending them. Whoever gathers against you will fall because of you.
“Look, I made the blacksmith who fans the coals till they blaze and hammers out a weapon for its work. I also made the destroyer who tears things down.
No weapon made against you will win. You'll prove every voice that accuses you in court wrong. That's the inheritance of the LORD's servants, and their righteousness comes from me,” says the LORD.
“Hey, everybody who's thirsty, come to the water! Even if you haven't got money, come buy and eat! Come get wine and milk. You don't need money. It costs you nothing.
Why spend money on stuff that isn't food or work for things that leave you empty? Listen closely to me and eat what's good. Let your soul enjoy the rich food.
Lean in and come to me. Listen and you'll live. I'll make a covenant with you that lasts forever, with the faithful love I promised David.
Look, I made him a witness for the peoples, a leader and commander over them.
Look, you'll call a nation you don't know, and a nation that didn't know you will run to you because of the LORD your God, the Holy One of Israel. He's given you glory.”
Look for the LORD while you can find him. Call out while he's close.

Let people who do evil leave their road behind and those who do wrong give up their thoughts. Let them come back to the LORD. He'll show them mercy. Come back to our God, because he'll forgive freely.
“My thoughts aren't your thoughts, and your ways aren't my ways,” says the LORD.
“Just as the heavens are high above the earth, my ways are higher than your ways and my thoughts higher than yours.
Rain and snow come down from the sky. They don't go back up before watering the earth, making things grow and sprout, giving seed to the planter and bread to the one who eats.
That's what my word is like when it leaves my mouth. It won't come back empty. It'll do what I want and succeed at what I sent it to do.
You'll go out with joy and be led along in peace. Mountains and hills will burst into song in front of you, and every tree in the field will clap its hands.
Cypress trees will rise where thorns grew. Myrtle will grow where briers were. It'll bring honor to the LORD's name, a sign that lasts forever and won't be cut off.”
The LORD says, “Keep justice going and do what's right. My salvation is close, and my righteousness is about to be revealed.
Blessed is anyone who does this and sticks to it, who keeps the Sabbath holy and keeps their hands from doing anything evil.”
A foreigner who's joined the LORD shouldn't say, “The LORD will cut me off from his people.” A eunuch shouldn't say, “Look at me, I'm a dried-up tree.”
The LORD says, “To the eunuchs who keep my Sabbaths, choose what makes me glad, and hold tight to my covenant,
I'll give them a memorial and a name inside my house and within my walls that's better than sons and daughters. I'll give them a name that lasts forever and won't be cut off.
And the foreigners who join the LORD to serve him and love his name, everyone who keeps from profaning the Sabbath and holds fast to my covenant,

I'll bring them to my holy mountain and make them glad in my house of prayer. I'll accept their burnt offerings and sacrifices on my altar. My house will be called a house of prayer for every people.”
The Lord GOD, who gathers Israel's outcasts, says, “I'll gather still more people to them, along with those I've already gathered.”
Come and devour, all you animals out in the fields and all you animals in the forest!
Israel's watchmen are blind. None of them knows what's going on. They're dogs that can't bark. They lie around dreaming and love to sleep.
Those dogs are greedy and never have enough. They're shepherds who don't understand. They've all gone their own way, each looking out for what they can get.
“Come on,” they say. “I'll get the wine, and we'll drink our fill of strong liquor! Tomorrow will be just like today, only even bigger.”
People who do right die, and nobody takes it to heart. Merciful people are taken away, and nobody stops to think that they're being taken away from the evil.
They enter into peace. Each person who lived upright rests in their own bed.
“But come here, you children of a sorceress, you offspring of adulterers and prostitutes.
Who are you making fun of? Who are you opening your mouth wide at and sticking your tongue out at? Aren't you children of rebellion, born of lies?
You work yourselves up among the oaks, under every green tree, and kill children down in the valleys under the cracks in the rocks.
The smooth stones in the valley are your share. Yes, that's what you've got. You've poured out drinks for them and brought them offerings. Am I supposed to be pleased with that?
You've set your bed on a high mountain, way up there. You went up to make sacrifices there too.

You've put your memorial behind the door and its posts. You exposed yourself to somebody besides me and climbed into bed. You made the bed bigger and struck a deal with them. You loved what you saw there.
You went to the king with oil and piled on the perfume. You sent your messengers far off and lowered yourself all the way to the grave.
You wore yourself out on those long roads, but you never said, ‘This is pointless.’ You found enough strength to keep going, so you didn't give up.
“Who scared you so much that you lied and forgot me, without even thinking of me? Haven't I stayed quiet for a long time, and you still don't fear me?
I'll expose what you call righteousness. As for what you've done, it won't help you.

When you cry for help, let the things you've collected save you. The wind will pick them up, and a breath will blow them all away. But anyone who runs to me for safety will possess the land and inherit my holy mountain.”
He'll say, “Build it up, build it up! Get the road ready! Clear away everything my people might trip over!”

This is what the One high above all says, the One who lives forever and whose name is Holy. “I live in the high and holy place, and also with people who are humble and sorry for the wrong they've done. I give life back to humble spirits and to hearts that are broken over their wrongs.
I won't keep arguing forever or stay angry for good. The spirits and lives I made would give out in front of me.
I was angry at his greedy wrongdoing and struck him. I turned away in my anger, but he kept straying down the road his own heart wanted.
I've seen the way he's lived, and I'll heal him. I'll lead him and bring comfort back to him and those who mourn with him.
I make these words grow on people's lips: ‘Peace, peace to the ones far away and the ones close by,’” says the LORD. “I'll heal them.”
But the wicked are like a restless sea that can't settle down, tossing up muck and mud.
“There's no peace for the wicked,” says my God.
“Shout it out! Don't hold back! Raise your voice like a trumpet! Tell my people how they've rebelled. Tell Jacob's family about their sins.

They look for me every day and act excited to learn my ways. They ask me for fair rulings as if they were a nation that did right and never walked away from their God's law. They love coming close to God.

They ask, ‘Why did we fast if you didn't even see? Why did we put ourselves through all that if you didn't notice?’ Look at you on the day you fast. You do whatever pleases you and push all your workers around.
Look, you fast and then fight and argue, throwing punches with wicked fists. A fast like the one you're doing today won't get your voice heard up high.
Is that the fast I chose, a day when people make themselves miserable? Is it just bowing your head like a reed and sitting on sackcloth and ashes? You call that a fast, a day the LORD would accept?
“Here's the fast I chose. Untie the chains of wickedness. Undo the straps of the yoke. Let the people you've been crushing go free. Break every yoke.
Share your bread with hungry people. Bring the poor who have nowhere to go into your home. When you see somebody without clothes, cover them. Don't turn away from your own flesh and blood.
Then your light will break out like morning, and your healing will come quickly. Your righteousness will go ahead of you, and the LORD's glory will guard you from behind.
Then you'll call and the LORD will answer. You'll cry for help and he'll say, ‘Here I am.’ Get rid of the yoke among you, quit pointing fingers, and stop talking wickedly.
Give yourself to feeding hungry people and meet the needs of those who are hurting. Then your light will rise in the dark and your gloom will become like noon.
The LORD will always guide you, give you what you need in dry places, and put strength in your bones. You'll be like a well-watered garden, like a spring that never runs dry.
Your people will rebuild the old ruins, raising foundations that have been there for generations. They'll call you the one who fixes what's broken in the walls and makes the streets livable again.

“Hold your feet back on the Sabbath. Leave your own pleasures alone on my holy day. Call the Sabbath a joy and treat the LORD's holy day with honor. Honor it by giving up your usual ways, your own pleasures, and your own talk.
Then you'll find your joy in the LORD. I'll make you ride over the high places of the earth and feed you with the inheritance of your father Jacob.” The LORD himself has spoken.
Look, the LORD's arm hasn't gotten too short to save, and his ear hasn't gotten too dull to hear.
Your wrongdoing put a wall between you and your God. Your sins made him hide his face from you so he won't listen.
Your hands are stained with blood and your fingers with wrongdoing. Your lips tell lies, and your tongue mutters evil.
Nobody brings a case fairly or argues it honestly. They lean on empty claims and tell lies. They come up with trouble and give birth to wrongdoing.
They hatch viper eggs and spin spiderwebs. Eat one of their eggs and you'll die. Crush one and a viper comes out.
Their webs won't make clothes. They can't cover themselves with what they've made. Everything they do is crooked, and their hands are busy with violence.
They run straight toward evil and hurry to spill innocent blood. Their minds are full of wrongdoing. They leave ruin and destruction along their roads.
They don't know the road to peace, and there's no justice where they walk. They've made their paths crooked. Anyone who walks them won't know peace.
That's why justice is far away from us and righteousness never catches up. We look for light and see darkness. We wait for brightness and walk in gloom.
We feel along the wall like blind people, feeling our way like people with no eyes. We trip at noon as if it were dusk. Among strong people we're like the dead.
We all roar like bears and moan like doves. We look for justice and there's none. We look for rescue and it's far away.
We've piled up wrongs in front of you, and our sins testify against us. We can't get away from what we've done. We know our wrongdoing.
We rebelled against the LORD and denied him. We turned away from following our God, talked oppression and revolt, cooked up lies in our hearts, and spoke them out loud.
Justice gets pushed backward, and righteousness stands way off. Truth has fallen flat in the street, and honesty can't get in.
Truth is nowhere to be found, and whoever walks away from evil makes themselves a target. The LORD saw it, and it bothered him that there was no justice.
He saw there was nobody to step in and was appalled that no one spoke up. So his own arm brought salvation, and his own righteousness held him up.
He put on righteousness like chest armor and salvation like a helmet. He dressed himself in vengeance and wrapped himself in zeal like a cloak.
He'll pay people back for what they've done, anger for those who oppose him and payback for his enemies. Even the islands will get what's due them.
From the west people will stand in awe of the LORD's name, and from where the sun rises they'll stand in awe of his glory. He'll come like a rushing stream driven by the LORD's breath.
“A Redeemer will come to Zion and to the people in Jacob who turn away from rebellion,” says the LORD.

“Here's my covenant with them,” says the LORD. “My Spirit is on you, and the words I've put in your mouth won't leave your lips, your children's lips, or your grandchildren's lips, from now on and forever,” says the LORD.
“Get up and shine! Your light has come, and the LORD's glory has risen over you!
Look, darkness will cover the earth, and deep darkness will cover the peoples. But the LORD will rise over you, and his glory will be visible on you.
Nations will come to your light, and kings will come to the brightness of your dawn.
“Look up and see what's happening all around you. They're all gathering and coming your way. Your sons will come from far off, and your daughters will be carried in people's arms.
You'll see it and light up. Your heart will race and swell with joy. The riches of the sea will come your way, and the wealth of the nations will come to you.
You'll be covered in camels, the one-humped camels of Midian and Ephah. People from Sheba will come with gold and frankincense, telling everyone about the LORD's praise.
All the flocks of Kedar will be gathered for you, and the rams of Nebaioth will serve you. I'll accept them on my altar and make my glorious house even more beautiful.
“Who are these flying in like a cloud, like doves coming back to their windows?

The islands will wait for me, with the ships of Tarshish out front, bringing your sons from far away with their silver and gold. They come for the name of the LORD your God and for the Holy One of Israel, because he's given you glory.
“Foreigners will rebuild your walls, and their kings will serve you. I struck you in my anger, but in my favor I've shown you mercy.
Your gates will stay open all the time. They won't shut day or night, so people can bring you the wealth of the nations, with their kings led in as captives.
Any nation or kingdom that refuses to serve you will perish. Those nations will be wiped out.
“The glory of Lebanon will come to you, cypress, pine, and box trees together, to make my sanctuary beautiful. I'll make the place where my feet rest glorious.
The children of those who crushed you will come bowing down. Everyone who looked down on you will bow at the soles of your feet. They'll call you the LORD's City, the Zion of the Holy One of Israel.
“You were left behind and hated, so empty nobody even passed through. I'll make you a lasting glory and a joy for generation after generation.
You'll drink the milk of nations and nurse at the breasts of royalty. Then you'll know that I, the LORD, am your Savior, your Redeemer, the Mighty One of Jacob.
I'll bring you gold in place of bronze and silver in place of iron, bronze in place of wood and iron in place of stone. I'll make peace your governor and righteousness your ruler.
You won't hear about violence in your land anymore, or ruin and destruction inside your borders. You'll call your walls Salvation and your gates Praise.
You won't need the sun to light your day or the moon to shine for you. The LORD will be your light forever, and your God will be your glory.
Your sun won't set anymore, and your moon won't disappear. The LORD will be your light forever, and your days of mourning will be over.
