All your people will do what's right. They'll inherit the land forever. They're the branch I planted and the work of my hands, so that I'll be glorified.
The smallest will become a thousand and the little one a strong nation. I, the LORD, will make it happen fast when its time comes.”

The Spirit of the Lord GOD is on me, because the LORD anointed me to bring good news to the humble. He sent me to bandage broken hearts, to announce freedom for captives and release for people tied up,
to announce the year of the LORD's favor and our God's day of vengeance, to comfort everyone who mourns,

to care for those grieving in Zion, giving them a crown in place of ashes, oil of joy in place of mourning, and clothes of praise in place of a heavy spirit. They'll be called trees of righteousness, planted by the LORD so he'll be glorified.
They'll rebuild the old ruins and raise up places that were wrecked long ago. They'll repair cities that have been desolate for generations.
Strangers will stand out there feeding your flocks. Foreigners will work your fields and vineyards.
But you'll be called the LORD's priests. People will call you servants of our God. You'll live on the wealth of the nations and take pride in their glory.
In place of shame you'll have a double share. In place of disgrace you'll celebrate what you receive. You'll own double in your land, and the joy you have will never end.
“I, the LORD, love justice. I hate robbery and wrongdoing. I'll give them what they've earned faithfully, and I'll make a covenant with them that lasts forever.
Their children will be known among the nations, and their descendants among the peoples. Everyone who sees them will recognize them as the family the LORD has blessed.”

I'm going to celebrate the LORD with everything I've got! My soul will find joy in my God. He's dressed me in clothes of salvation and wrapped me in a robe of righteousness, like a groom putting on his crown or a bride getting dressed in her jewels.
Just like the earth pushes up new shoots and a garden makes the seeds in it sprout, the Lord GOD will make righteousness and praise spring up right in front of all the nations.
For Zion's sake I won't stay quiet. For Jerusalem's sake I won't rest till her righteousness shines like dawn and her salvation burns like a lamp.
Nations will see your righteousness and every king will see your glory. You'll have a new name the LORD himself gives you.
You'll be a beautiful crown in the LORD's hand, a royal crown held by your God.
Nobody will call you Forsaken anymore, and nobody will call your land Desolate. They'll call you Hephzibah and your land Beulah, because the LORD delights in you and your land will be married.
As a young man marries a young woman, your sons will marry you. The way a groom celebrates his bride is how your God will celebrate you.
Jerusalem, I've put watchmen on your walls. They won't go quiet day or night. You who call on the LORD, don't take a break,
and don't give him a break till he makes Jerusalem stand firm and makes the whole earth praise her.
The LORD swore by his right hand and his mighty arm, “I won't give your grain to your enemies to eat anymore, and strangers won't drink the new wine you worked for.
The people who harvest the grain will eat it and praise the LORD. The people who gather the grapes will drink the wine in the courts of my sanctuary.”
Go through the gates! Get the road ready for the people! Build up the highway! Clear the stones out of the way and raise a banner for the peoples.
Look, the LORD has announced it all the way to the ends of the earth: “Tell daughter Zion, ‘Look, your salvation is coming! His reward is with him, and what he'll give in return goes ahead of him!’”
People will call them “The Holy People, The LORD's Redeemed.” You'll be called “Sought Out, A City Not Forsaken.”

Who's this coming from Edom, from Bozrah with clothes stained red? Who's this in splendid clothes, striding forward in all his strength? “It's me. I speak what's right, and I've got the power to save.”
Why are your clothes red, like what someone wears when they stomp grapes in a wine vat?

“I stomped the winepress alone. Nobody from the peoples was there with me. I stomped them in my anger and trampled them in my fury. Their lifeblood splashed across my clothes, and everything I'm wearing is stained.
The day to take vengeance was in my heart, and the year for my redeemed had come.
I looked around and nobody was there to help. I was stunned that nobody stood with me. So my own arm brought me victory, and my own anger kept me going.
I trampled the peoples in my anger and made them drunk in my fury. I poured their lifeblood out on the ground.”
I'll talk about the LORD's faithful love and give him praise for everything he's given us. I'll tell of the great good he's done for Israel's family out of his mercy and all his faithful love.
He said, “Surely they're my people, children who won't deal falsely with me.” So he became their Savior.
All their suffering hurt him too, and the angel of his presence saved them. In love and compassion he bought them back. He lifted them up and carried them through all those days long ago.
But they rebelled and grieved his Holy Spirit. So he turned against them and fought them himself.
Then he remembered the old days, Moses and his people. “Where's the one who brought them up out of the sea with the shepherds of his flock? Where's the one who put his Holy Spirit among them?”
Who put his glorious arm at Moses' right hand? Who split the waters ahead of them to make a name for himself that would last forever?
Who led them through the deep like a horse through open country, so they didn't trip?
Like cattle going down into a valley, they found rest because the LORD's Spirit gave it to them. That's how you led your people and made your name glorious.
Look down from heaven, from the place where you live in holiness and glory. Where's your zeal? Where are the mighty things you used to do? You've held back your deep love and compassion from me.
You're our Father, even if Abraham doesn't know us and Israel won't claim us. You, LORD, are our Father. Your name from forever is Our Redeemer.
LORD, why do you let us wander from your roads and harden our hearts so we don't fear you? Come back for your servants, the tribes that belong to you.
Your holy people held the land for only a little while. Our enemies have trampled your sanctuary.
We've become like people you never ruled, people who never carried your name.
If only you'd rip the heavens open and come down, so mountains would shake when you showed up!
Come like a fire that catches in brush and makes water boil. Make your name known to your enemies so the nations shake in front of you.
When you did amazing things we never saw coming, you came down and mountains shook in your presence.
Since long ago nobody has heard or seen a God besides you who acts for people who wait for him.
You meet people who gladly do what's right, who remember you by walking your roads. Look, you were angry, and we sinned. We've been stuck in sin a long time. Can we be saved?
We've all become like somebody unclean, and even the right things we do are like dirty clothes. We all wither like leaves, and our wrongdoing carries us off like the wind.
Nobody calls on your name or gets up to grab hold of you. You've hidden your face from us and let our wrongdoing eat us up.
But LORD, you're still our Father. We're the clay and you're the potter. Every one of us is the work of your hands.
LORD, don't stay furious. Don't remember our wrongs forever. Please look at us. We're all your people.
Your holy cities have become wilderness. Zion is a wasteland, and Jerusalem lies in ruins.
Our beautiful, holy house where our ancestors praised you has burned down. Every place we loved is wrecked.
LORD, will you hold back after all this? Will you stay quiet and keep punishing us so hard?
“I let people ask me who hadn't asked before. I let people find me who weren't looking. I said, ‘Here I am! Here I am!’ to a nation that didn't carry my name.
All day I held out my hands to rebellious people who walk a road that leads to no good, following whatever comes into their heads.
They keep provoking me to my face, offering sacrifices in gardens and burning incense on bricks.
They sit among graves and spend the night in secret places. They eat pork and keep broth from disgusting things in their pots.
They tell people, ‘Stay over there. Don't come close. I'm holier than you.’ They're like smoke in my nose, like a fire burning all day.
“Look, it's written right in front of me. I won't stay quiet. I'll pay them back, putting it right into their laps,

for your wrongs and your ancestors' wrongs together,” says the LORD. “They burned incense on the mountains and insulted me on the hills. I'll measure out what their past deeds earned and put it right in their laps.”
The LORD says, “When there's juice in a bunch of grapes, someone says, ‘Don't crush the whole thing. There's a blessing in it.’ That's what I'll do for my servants so they won't all be destroyed.
I'll bring descendants out of Jacob and someone out of Judah to inherit my mountains. My chosen people will inherit the land, and my servants will live there.
Sharon will be a place for sheep, and the valley of Achor a place where herds lie down, for my people who came looking for me.
“But you walked away from the LORD. You forgot my holy mountain, set a table for Fortune, and filled cups with mixed wine for Destiny.

I'll give you the sword for your destiny, and you'll all bow down to be slaughtered. I called and you didn't answer. I spoke and you didn't listen. You did what was evil in my eyes and chose what I take no pleasure in.”
So the Lord GOD says, “Look, my servants will eat and you'll be hungry. My servants will drink and you'll be thirsty. My servants will celebrate and you'll end up ashamed.
My servants will sing with glad hearts. You'll cry from a hurting heart and wail because your spirit is crushed.
You'll leave your name behind as a curse my chosen people can use, and the Lord GOD will put you to death. He'll give his servants another name.
Then whoever asks for a blessing on earth will ask the God of truth, and whoever swears on earth will swear by the God of truth. The old troubles will be forgotten and out of my sight.
“Look, I'm making new heavens and a new earth. What came before won't be remembered. It won't even come to mind.
Be glad and celebrate forever over what I create. Look, I'm making Jerusalem a delight and her people a joy.
I'll celebrate Jerusalem and take joy in my people. Nobody will hear crying or weeping there anymore.

“No baby there will live only a few days, and no old person will die without living out their years. Someone who dies at a hundred will still be considered young, and a sinner who reaches a hundred will be considered cursed.
They'll build houses and get to live in them. They'll plant vineyards and eat the fruit themselves.
They won't build for somebody else to live there or plant for somebody else to eat. My people will live as long as trees, and my chosen ones will enjoy what they've made for a long time.
Their hard work won't go to waste, and they won't have children just to see disaster hit them. They're the family the LORD blessed, and so are their children with them.
Before they even call, I'll answer. While they're still speaking, I'll hear.
Wolves and lambs will feed together. Lions will eat straw like oxen, and snakes will eat dust. No one will harm or destroy anywhere on my holy mountain,” says the LORD.
The LORD says, “Heaven is my throne and the earth is where I rest my feet. What kind of house are you going to build me? Where could I settle down?

My hand made everything you see. That's how it all came to be,” says the LORD. “Here's the person I pay attention to: someone poor and brokenhearted over their wrongs, someone who trembles at my word.

The one who kills an ox is like someone who kills a person. The one who sacrifices a lamb is like someone who breaks a dog's neck. The one bringing an offering is like someone offering pig's blood. The one burning frankincense is like someone blessing an idol. They chose their own ways and deep down love those disgusting things.
So I'll choose what deceives them and bring their fears down on them. When I called, nobody answered. When I spoke, nobody listened. They did what's evil in my eyes and chose what doesn't please me.”

Listen to the LORD's word, you who tremble at what he says. “Your own people hate you and throw you out because of my name. They say, ‘Let the LORD get glory so we can see your joy.’ They'll be the ones who end up ashamed.
“Hear that roar from the city, that voice from the temple! It's the LORD paying back his enemies what they deserve.
“Before she went into labor, she gave birth. Before the pain came, she delivered a son.
Who's ever heard of that? Who's seen anything like it? Can a country be born in a single day? Can a nation come to life all at once? As soon as Zion went into labor, she gave birth to her children.
Would I bring somebody to the point of birth and then stop the delivery?” says the LORD. “Would I, the one who makes birth happen, shut the womb?” says your God.
“Celebrate with Jerusalem, all you who love her. Be happy for her! Celebrate with her, all you who grieved over her.
Then you'll nurse and get your fill at the breasts that comfort you. You'll drink deeply and enjoy the fullness of her glory.”
The LORD says, “Look, I'll send peace flowing to her like a river, and the glory of the nations like a stream overflowing its banks. You'll nurse, be carried on her hip, and bounce on her knees.
I'll comfort you the way a mother comforts her child. You'll find comfort in Jerusalem.”
You'll see it and your heart will leap. Your bones will thrive like fresh grass. The LORD's hand will be made known to his servants, and he'll show anger to his enemies.
Look, the LORD is coming with fire. His chariots will come like a whirlwind. He'll bring his fierce anger and rebuke with blazing flames.
The LORD will judge all people with fire and his sword, and many will be struck down by him.
“Those who make themselves holy and clean for the gardens and follow the one in the middle, eating pork, disgusting things, and mice, will all come to an end together,” says the LORD.
“I know what they do and what they think. The time is coming to gather every nation and language. They'll come and see my glory.

“I'll set a sign among them and send survivors out to the nations, to Tarshish, Pul, and Lud, the people who draw the bow, to Tubal and Javan, and to far-off islands that haven't heard of me or seen my glory. They'll tell those nations about my glory.

They'll bring all your brothers and sisters from every nation as an offering to the LORD. They'll come on horses, in chariots, on carrying chairs, and on mules and camels to my holy mountain, Jerusalem,” says the LORD, “just as Israel brings an offering in a clean vessel to the LORD's house.
I'll even choose some of them to be priests and Levites,” says the LORD.
“The new heavens and the new earth I'm going to make will stand before me,” says the LORD. “That's how your descendants and your name will last.
From one new moon to the next, and from one Sabbath to the next, everyone will come to worship in front of me,” says the LORD.
“They'll go outside and see the bodies of the people who rebelled against me. The worms feeding on them won't die, the fire burning them won't go out, and everyone will be horrified by them.”
